title.zh: 卷二百一十九 列傳第一百四十四 北狄
title.raw: 卷二百一十九 列傳第一百四十四 北狄 Volume 219 Biographies 144: Beidi

sentences.zh: 契丹 奚 室韋 靺鞨渤海

translations.literal: Khitan, Xi, Shiwei, Mohe, Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: Khitan, Xi, Shiwei, Mohe, and Bohai.

sentences.zh: 契丹，本東胡種，其先爲匈奴所破，保鮮卑山。

translations.literal: The Khitan were originally of the Eastern Hu stock; their ancestors were defeated by the Xiongnu and took refuge in the Xianbei Mountains.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan were originally an Eastern Hu people. After their forebears were broken by the Xiongnu, they held to the Xianbei Mountains.

sentences.zh: 魏青龍中，部酋比能稍桀驁，爲幽州刺史王雄所殺，衆遂微，逃潢水之南，黃龍之北。

translations.literal: In the Qinglong era of Wei, the tribal chief Binen grew somewhat arrogant and defiant and was killed by Wang Xiong, governor of Youzhou; the multitude then dwindled and fled south of the Huangshui River and north of Huanglong.
translations.idiomatic: During Wei’s Qinglong reign, the tribal chief Binen grew increasingly unruly until Wang Xiong, governor of Youzhou, killed him. The people then weakened and withdrew south of the Huangshui and north of Huanglong.

sentences.zh: 至元魏，自號曰契丹。

translations.literal: Reaching the Northern Wei, they styled themselves Khitan.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Northern Wei they took the name Khitan for themselves.

sentences.zh: 地直京師東北五千里而贏，東距高麗，西奚，南營州，北靺鞨、室韋，阻冷陘山以自固。

translations.literal: Their territory lay straight northeast of the capital five thousand li away and more, east bordering Goguryeo, west the Xi, south Yingzhou, north Mohe and Shiwei, relying on Lengxing Mountain to secure themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Their lands lay some five thousand li northeast of the capital, bordering Goguryeo on the east, the Xi on the west, Yingzhou on the south, and Mohe and Shiwei on the north, with Lengxing Mountain as their natural rampart.

sentences.zh: 射獵居處無常。

translations.literal: They hunted with bow and lived in no fixed places.
translations.idiomatic: They lived by hunting and moved their camps without fixed abodes.

sentences.zh: 其君大賀氏，有勝兵四萬，析八部，臣於突厥，以爲俟斤。

translations.literal: Their ruler was of the Dahe clan; they had forty thousand seasoned troops, were divided into eight tribes, and submitted to the Turks, by whom they were made irkin.
translations.idiomatic: Their ruling house was the Dahe clan. They fielded forty thousand seasoned warriors, were organized in eight tribes, and submitted to the Turks, who appointed them an irkin.

sentences.zh: 凡調發攻戰，則諸部畢會；

translations.literal: Whenever mobilized for attack or war, all the tribes would assemble.
translations.idiomatic: When called to war or raiding, every tribe had to muster.

sentences.zh: 獵則部得自行。

translations.literal: For hunting, each tribe could act on its own.
translations.idiomatic: On the hunt, each tribe went its own way.

sentences.zh: 與奚不平，每鬥不利，輒遁保鮮卑山。

translations.literal: They were at odds with the Xi; whenever they fought and fared poorly, they would flee and hold to the Xianbei Mountains.
translations.idiomatic: They were at odds with the Xi, and whenever they fought and lost, they would withdraw to the shelter of the Xianbei Mountains.

sentences.zh: 風俗與突厥大抵略侔。

translations.literal: Their customs were on the whole roughly similar to those of the Turks.
translations.idiomatic: Their customs were, in the main, much like those of the Turks.

sentences.zh: 死不墓，以馬車載屍入山，置於樹顛。

translations.literal: They did not bury the dead in graves but carried the corpse into the mountains in a horse cart and placed it atop a tree.
translations.idiomatic: They did not bury their dead in graves but carried the corpse into the mountains in a cart and set it in the crown of a tree.

sentences.zh: 子孫死，父母旦夕哭；

translations.literal: When children died, the parents wept morning and evening.
translations.idiomatic: When a child died, the parents mourned morning and evening.

sentences.zh: 父母死則否，亦無喪期。

translations.literal: When parents died they did not, and there was no mourning period either.
translations.idiomatic: When parents died they did not, and they observed no fixed mourning period.

sentences.zh: 武德中，其大酋孫敖曹與靺鞨長突地稽俱遣人來朝，而君長或小入寇邊。

translations.literal: In the Wude era, their great chief Sun Aocao and the Mohe leader Tudi Ji both sent men to court, while lesser chiefs sometimes raided the border in small bands.
translations.idiomatic: During the Wude reign, the great Khitan chief Sun Aocao and the Mohe leader Tudi Ji both sent envoys to court, though lesser chiefs still made small border raids from time to time.

sentences.zh: 後二年，君長乃遣使者上名馬、豐貂。

translations.literal: Two years later the chieftain sent envoys presenting famed horses and rich sable.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later the chieftain sent envoys bearing famed horses and rich sable pelts.

sentences.zh: 貞觀二年，摩會來降。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenguan, Mohui came to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhenguan, Mohui came over to the Tang side.

sentences.zh: 突厥頡利可汗不欲外夷與唐合，乃請以梁師都易契丹。

translations.literal: The Türk qaghan Jieli did not wish outer tribes to join with Tang and asked to exchange Liang Shidu for the Khitan.
translations.idiomatic: The Türk qaghan Jieli did not want outer tribes allying with Tang and asked to trade Liang Shidu for the Khitan.

sentences.zh: 太宗曰：「契丹、突厥不同類，今已降我，尚可索邪？

translations.literal: The Emperor Taizong said: "The Khitan and the Turks are not of one kind; they have now submitted to us—can they still be demanded?"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong replied: "The Khitan and the Turks are not one people. They have already submitted to us—how can they still be demanded back?"

sentences.zh: 師都，唐編戶，盜我州部，突厥輒爲助，我將禽之，誼不可易降者。

translations.literal: "As for Shidu, he is a Tang registered household who plunders our prefectures and districts, and the Turks always aid him; we mean to capture him, and it is not right to exchange him for those who have surrendered."
translations.idiomatic: "As for Shidu, he is a man of our registered households who raids our prefectures, and the Turks always back him. We intend to take him, and it would be wrong to trade surrendered men for him."

sentences.zh: 」明年，摩會復入朝，賜鼓纛，由是有常貢。

translations.literal: "The next year Mohui came to court again and was given drums and banners, and thereafter there were regular tribute missions.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Mohui came to court again and was given drums and banners, after which regular tribute missions followed.

sentences.zh: 帝伐高麗，悉發酋長與奚首領從軍。

translations.literal: When the Emperor campaigned against Goguryeo, he mobilized all the chieftains and the Xi leaders to follow the army.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor marched against Goguryeo, he called up every Khitan chieftain and Xi leader to join the campaign.

sentences.zh: 帝還，過營州，盡召其長窟哥及老人，差賜繒采，以窟哥爲左武衛將軍。

translations.literal: On his return he passed through Yingzhou, summoned all the elders including the chief Kuge, bestowed silks in differing amounts, and appointed Kuge Left Martial Guard General.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he passed through Yingzhou, summoned Kuge and the other elders, gave them graded gifts of silk, and made Kuge Left Martial Guard General.

sentences.zh: 大酋辱紇主曲據又率衆歸，即其部爲玄州，拜曲據刺史，隸營州都督府。

translations.literal: The great chief Ruhuo Zhuzhuquju again led his people to submit; his tribe was made Xuanzhou, Quju was appointed prefect, and it was placed under the Yingzhou Protectorate.
translations.idiomatic: The great chief Ruhuo Zhuzhuquju again led his people in submission. His tribe was made Xuanzhou, Quju was made prefect, and the district was placed under the Yingzhou Protectorate.

sentences.zh: 未幾，窟哥舉部內屬，乃置松漠都督府，以窟哥爲使持節十州諸軍事、松漠都督，封無極男，賜氏李。

translations.literal: Before long Kuge brought his whole tribe within the borders; the Songmo Protectorate was then established, with Kuge as commissioner bearing the staff of authority over the military affairs of ten prefectures and as Songmo Protector, enfeoffed as Lord of Wuji, and granted the surname Li.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Kuge brought his entire tribe within the borders. The Songmo Protectorate was then set up, with Kuge as commissioner with staff of authority over ten prefectures’ military affairs and as Songmo protector, enfeoffed as Lord of Wuji and granted the surname Li.

sentences.zh: 以達稽部爲峭落州，紇便部爲彈汗州，獨活部爲無逢州，芬問部爲羽陵州，突便部爲日連州，芮奚部爲徒河州，墜斤部爲萬丹州，伏部爲匹黎、赤山二州，俱隸松漠府，即以辱紇主爲之刺史。

translations.literal: The Daji tribe was made Qiaoluo Prefecture, the Hebian tribe Tanhan Prefecture, the Duhuo tribe Wufeng Prefecture, the Fenwen tribe Yuling Prefecture, the Tubian tribe Rilian Prefecture, the Ruixi tribe Tuhe Prefecture, the Zhuijin tribe Wandan Prefecture, and the Fu tribe the two prefectures of Pili and Chishan—all subordinate to Songmo, with Ruhuo Zhuzhu as their prefect.
translations.idiomatic: The Daji tribe became Qiaoluo Prefecture, the Hebian Tanhan, the Duhuo Wufeng, the Fenwen Yuling, the Tubian Rilian, the Ruixi Tuhe, the Zhuijin Wandan, and the Fu tribe the two prefectures of Pili and Chishan—all under Songmo, with Ruhuo Zhuzhu as their prefect.

sentences.zh: 窟哥死，與奚連叛，行軍總管阿史德樞賓等執松漠都督阿卜固獻東都。

translations.literal: When Kuge died he rebelled together with the Xi; the campaign commander Ashide Shubin and others seized the Songmo Protector Abu and presented him at the eastern capital.
translations.idiomatic: After Kuge died they rebelled together with the Xi. The campaign commander Ashide Shubin and others seized the Songmo protector Abu and sent him to the eastern capital.

sentences.zh: 窟哥有二孫：曰枯莫離，爲左衛將軍、彈汗州刺史，封歸順郡王；

translations.literal: Kuge had two grandsons: one named Kumoli, Left Guard General and prefect of Tanhan, enfeoffed Duke of Guishun;
translations.idiomatic: Kuge had two grandsons: Kumoli, who was Left Guard General and prefect of Tanhan, enfeoffed as Duke of Guishun;

sentences.zh: 曰盡忠，爲武衛大將軍、松漠都督。

translations.literal: the other named Jinzhong, Grand General of the Martial Guard and Songmo Protector.
translations.idiomatic: and Jinzhong, Grand General of the Martial Guard and Songmo protector.

sentences.zh: 而敖曹有孫曰萬榮，爲歸誠州刺史。

translations.literal: Aocao had a grandson named Wanrong, who was prefect of Guicheng.
translations.idiomatic: Aocao had a grandson named Wanrong, who served as prefect of Guicheng.

sentences.zh: 於是營州都督趙文翽驕遝，數侵侮其下，盡忠等皆怨望。

translations.literal: The Yingzhou Protector Zhao Wenshu was arrogant and overbearing and repeatedly insulted his subordinates, and Jinzhong and the others all harbored resentment.
translations.idiomatic: The Yingzhou protector Zhao Wenshu was arrogant and overbearing and repeatedly humiliated his subordinates, and Jinzhong and the others all nursed grievances.

sentences.zh: 萬榮本以侍子入朝，知中國險易，挾亂不疑，即共舉兵，殺文翽，盜營州反。

translations.literal: Wanrong had entered court as a hostage attendant and knew the strengths and weaknesses of China; trusting in disorder, he did not hesitate, and together they raised troops, killed Wenshu, seized Yingzhou, and rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Wanrong had come to court as a hostage attendant and knew China’s strengths and weaknesses. Trusting that turmoil would serve him, he joined them without hesitation. Together they rose, killed Wenshu, seized Yingzhou, and rebelled.

sentences.zh: 盡忠自號無上可汗，以萬榮爲將，縱兵四略，所向輒下，不重浹，衆數萬，妄言十萬，攻崇州，執討擊副使許欽寂。

translations.literal: Jinzhong styled himself Supreme Qaghan and made Wanrong his general; they drove their troops in all directions, and wherever they went they took the place; they did not pause to rest, their numbers reaching tens of thousands while they falsely claimed a hundred thousand; they attacked Chongzhou and captured the punitive deputy commissioner Xu Qinji.
translations.idiomatic: Jinzhong styled himself Supreme Qaghan and made Wanrong his general. They drove their forces in every direction and took whatever they met without pausing. Their numbers ran to tens of thousands while they boasted of a hundred thousand. They attacked Chongzhou and captured the punitive deputy commissioner Xu Qinji.

sentences.zh: 武后怒，詔鷹揚將軍曹仁師、金吾大將軍張玄遇、右武威大將軍李多祚、司農少卿麻仁節等二十八將擊之；

translations.literal: Empress Wu was enraged and ordered the Hawk-Flying General Cao Renshi, the Golden Guard Grand General Zhang Xuanyu, the Right Martial Guard Grand General Li Duozuo, the Minister of Agriculture Vice Minister Ma Renjie, and twenty-eight other generals to strike them;
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu was furious and ordered the Hawk-Flying General Cao Renshi, the Golden Guard Grand General Zhang Xuanyu, the Right Martial Guard Grand General Li Duozuo, the Vice Minister of Agriculture Ma Renjie, and twenty-eight other generals to attack them;

sentences.zh: 以梁王武三思爲榆關道安撫大使，納言姚璹爲之副。

translations.literal: with Prince of Liang Wu Sansi as pacification commissioner of the Yuguan route and Censor-in-Chief Yao Shuang as his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: with the Prince of Liang Wu Sansi as pacification commissioner of the Yuguan route and Censor-in-Chief Yao Shuang as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 更號萬榮曰萬斬，盡忠曰盡滅。

translations.literal: Wanrong was renamed Wan Zhan and Jinzhong renamed Jin Mie.
translations.idiomatic: Wanrong was renamed Wan Zhan and Jinzhong Jin Mie.

sentences.zh: 諸將戰西硤石黃麞谷，王師敗績，玄遇、仁節皆爲虜禽。

translations.literal: The generals fought at Huangzhang Valley west of Xiashi; the imperial army was defeated and Xuanyu and Renjie were both captured.
translations.idiomatic: The generals fought at Huangzhang Valley west of Xiashi. The imperial army was routed, and Xuanyu and Renjie were both taken captive.

sentences.zh: 進攻平州，不克。

translations.literal: They advanced to attack Pingzhou but could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: They pressed on to attack Pingzhou but could not capture it.

sentences.zh: 敗書聞，后乃以右武衛大將軍建安王武攸宜爲清邊道大總管，擊契丹；

translations.literal: When word of defeat arrived, the Empress then appointed the Right Martial Guard Grand General Prince of Jian’an Wu Youyi as grand general of the Qingbian route to strike the Khitan;
translations.idiomatic: When news of defeat arrived, the empress appointed the Right Martial Guard Grand General Prince of Jian’an Wu Youyi grand general of the Qingbian route to strike the Khitan;

sentences.zh: 募天下人奴有勇者，官畀主直，悉發以擊虜。

translations.literal: she recruited brave men from among slaves throughout the realm, paid their masters their price, and sent them all to strike the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: she recruited brave men from among slaves throughout the realm, paid their masters their price, and sent them all against the enemy.

sentences.zh: 萬榮銜枚夜襲檀州，清邊道副總管張九節募死士數百薄戰，萬榮敗而走山。

translations.literal: Wanrong attacked Tanzhou by night with gags in their mouths; the Qingbian route deputy grand general Zhang Jiujie mustered several hundred death-fighters for a close fight, and Wanrong was defeated and fled into the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Wanrong attacked Tanzhou by night with gags in their mouths. The Qingbian deputy grand general Zhang Jiujie mustered several hundred death-fighters for close combat, and Wanrong was beaten and fled into the hills.

sentences.zh: 俄而盡忠死，突厥默啜襲破其部。

translations.literal: Before long Jinzhong died and the Türk qaghan Mojie smashed his tribe.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Jinzhong died, and the Türk qaghan Mojie shattered his tribe.

sentences.zh: 萬榮收散兵復振，使別將駱務整、何阿小入冀州，殺刺史陸寶積，掠數千人。

translations.literal: Wanrong gathered the scattered troops and revived his power, sending his lieutenants Luo Wuzheng and He Axiao into Jizhou, where they killed the prefect Lu Baoji and carried off several thousand people.
translations.idiomatic: Wanrong gathered the scattered troops and revived his strength, sending his lieutenants Luo Wuzheng and He Axiao into Jizhou, where they killed Prefect Lu Baoji and carried off several thousand people.

sentences.zh: 武后聞盡忠死，更詔夏官尚書王孝傑、羽林衛將軍蘇宏暉率兵十七萬討契丹，戰東硤石，師敗，孝傑死之。

translations.literal: When the Empress heard that Jinzhong was dead she again ordered the Minister of Summer Works Wang Xiaojie and the Feathered Forest Guard General Su Honghui to lead one hundred seventy thousand troops to punish the Khitan; they fought east of Xiashi, the army was defeated, and Xiaojie died.
translations.idiomatic: When the empress heard that Jinzhong was dead, she again ordered the Minister of Summer Works Wang Xiaojie and the Feathered Forest Guard General Su Honghui to lead one hundred seventy thousand men against the Khitan. They fought east of Xiashi, the army was routed, and Xiaojie was killed.

sentences.zh: 萬榮席已勝，遂屠幽州。

translations.literal: Wanrong, presuming on victory already won, then massacred Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Presuming on victory already won, Wanrong then massacred Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 攸宜遣將討捕，不能克。

translations.literal: Youyi sent generals to pursue and capture them but could not overcome them.
translations.idiomatic: Youyi sent generals in pursuit but could not overcome them.

sentences.zh: 乃命右金吾衛大將軍河內郡王武懿宗爲神兵道大總管，右肅政台御史大夫婁師德爲清邊道大總管，右武威衛大將軍沙吒忠義爲清邊中道前軍總管，兵凡二十萬擊賊。

translations.literal: She then appointed the Right Golden Guard Grand General Prince of Henei Wu Yizong as grand general of the Divine Troops route, the Right Censorate Grand Censor Lou Shide as grand general of the Qingbian route, and the Right Martial Guard Grand General Shazha Zhongyi as front commander of the central Qingbian route, the army totaling two hundred thousand to strike the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: She then appointed the Right Golden Guard Grand General Prince of Henei Wu Yizong grand general of the Divine Troops route, the Right Censorate Grand Censor Lou Shide grand general of the Qingbian route, and the Right Martial Guard Grand General Shazha Zhongyi front commander of the central Qingbian route—two hundred thousand troops in all—to strike the rebels.

sentences.zh: 萬榮銳甚，鼓而南，殘瀛州屬縣，恣肆無所憚。

translations.literal: Wanrong was very sharp and, beating drums, drove south, ravaging the counties subordinate to Yingzhou and rampaging without restraint.
translations.idiomatic: Wanrong was at the height of his power. Beating drums, he drove south, ravaging the counties under Yingzhou and rampaging without restraint.

sentences.zh: 於是神兵道總管楊玄基率奚軍掩其尾，契丹大敗，獲何阿小，降別將李楷固、駱務整，收仗械如積。

translations.literal: Then the Divine Troops route commander Yang Xuanji led Xi troops to strike their rear; the Khitan were greatly defeated, He Axiao was captured, and the lieutenants Li Kaigu and Luo Wuzheng surrendered; weapons and gear were gathered in heaps.
translations.idiomatic: Then the Divine Troops route commander Yang Xuanji led Xi troops against their rear. The Khitan were routed, He Axiao was captured, and the lieutenants Li Kaigu and Luo Wuzheng surrendered. Captured arms and gear piled up like hills.

sentences.zh: 萬榮委軍走，殘隊復合，與奚搏。

translations.literal: Wanrong abandoned his army and fled; the remnant bands gathered again and fought the Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Wanrong abandoned his army and fled. The remnant bands gathered again and fought the Xi.

sentences.zh: 奚四面攻，乃大潰，萬榮左馳。

translations.literal: The Xi attacked from all four sides and they were utterly routed; Wanrong fled to the left.
translations.idiomatic: The Xi attacked from all four sides and broke them utterly. Wanrong fled to the left.

sentences.zh: 張九節爲三伏伺之，萬榮窮，與家奴輕騎走潞河東，憊甚，臥林下，奴斬其首，九節傳之東都，餘衆潰。

translations.literal: Zhang Jiujie set three ambushes and waited; Wanrong, at the end of his resources, fled east of the Lu River with a light escort, utterly exhausted; he lay down under the trees, and his slave cut off his head; Jiujie sent it to the eastern capital and the rest scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jiujie laid three ambushes and waited. Wanrong, at the end of his strength, fled east of the Lu River with only a light escort, utterly spent. He lay down under the trees, and his slave cut off his head. Jiujie sent it to the eastern capital, and the rest scattered.

sentences.zh: 攸宜凱而還，后喜，爲赦天下，改元爲神功。

translations.literal: Youyi returned in triumph, and the Empress rejoiced and amnestied the realm, changing the reign title to Shendong.
translations.idiomatic: Youyi returned in triumph. The empress rejoiced, amnestied the realm, and changed the reign title to Shendong.

sentences.zh: 開元二年，盡忠從父弟都督失活以默啜政衰，率部落與頡利發伊健啜來歸，玄宗賜丹書鐵券。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kaiyuan, the protector Shihuo, Jinzhong’s cousin on the father’s side, because Mojie’s power was declining, led his tribe and the Yili qaghan Yijian Kuli to submit; Emperor Xuanzong bestowed a red-document iron tally.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Kaiyuan, the protector Shihuo—Jinzhong’s cousin on the father’s side—seeing that Mojie’s power was waning, led his tribe and the Yili qaghan Yijian Kuli to submit. Emperor Xuanzong bestowed a red-document iron tally.

sentences.zh: 後二年，與奚長李大酺皆來，詔復置松漠府，以失活爲都督，封松漠郡王，授左金吾衛大將軍。

translations.literal: Two years later he came together with the Xi chieftain Li Dapu; an edict restored the Songmo Protectorate, with Shihuo as protector, enfeoffed Prince of Songmo, and appointed Left Golden Guard Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later he came together with the Xi chieftain Li Dapu. An edict restored the Songmo Protectorate, made Shihuo protector and Prince of Songmo, and appointed him Left Golden Guard Grand General.

sentences.zh: 仍其府置靜析軍，以失活爲經略大使，所統八部皆擢其酋爲刺史。

translations.literal: The Jingxi Army was still set at his protectorate, with Shihuo as frontier commissioner; all eight tribes under him had their chiefs promoted to prefect.
translations.idiomatic: The Jingxi Army remained at his protectorate, with Shihuo as frontier commissioner. Every chief of the eight tribes under him was promoted to prefect.

sentences.zh: 詔將軍薛泰爲押蕃落使，督軍鎮撫。

translations.literal: An edict made the general Xue Tai commissioner for overseeing the tribal settlements, supervising troops to pacify and guard.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed General Xue Tai commissioner for overseeing the tribal settlements, to supervise troops in pacification and defense.

sentences.zh: 帝以東平王外孫楊元嗣女爲永樂公主，妻失活。

translations.literal: The Emperor gave Yang Yuansi, daughter of the Prince of Dongping’s grandson, as the Princess of Yongle to wife Shihuo.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor gave Yang Yuansi, daughter of the Prince of Dongping’s grandson, as Princess of Yongle to be Shihuo’s wife.

sentences.zh: 明年，失活死，贈特進，帝遣使吊祠，以其弟中郎將娑固襲封及所領。

translations.literal: The next year Shihuo died; he was posthumously honored Special Advancement, and the Emperor sent envoys to mourn and sacrifice; his younger brother, Gentleman of the Palace Suogu, inherited the enfeoffment and what he had led.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Shihuo died and was posthumously honored Special Advancement. The emperor sent envoys to mourn and sacrifice. His younger brother Suogu, a gentleman of the palace, inherited the title and command.

sentences.zh: 明年，娑固與公主來朝，宴齎有加。

translations.literal: The next year Suogu came to court with the princess; the feast and gifts were especially generous.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Suogu came to court with the princess, and the feast and gifts were especially generous.

sentences.zh: 有可突於者，爲靜析軍副使，悍勇得衆，娑固欲去之，未決。

translations.literal: There was one Ketuyu, deputy of the Jingxi Army, fierce and brave and holding the multitude; Suogu wished to remove him but had not decided.
translations.idiomatic: There was one Ketuyu, deputy of the Jingxi Army, fierce and brave and holding the people’s loyalty. Suogu wished to remove him but had not yet decided.

sentences.zh: 可突於反攻娑固，娑固奔營州。

translations.literal: Ketuyu turned and attacked Suogu, who fled to Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ketuyu turned back against Suogu, who fled to Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 都督許欽澹以州甲五百，合奚君長李大酺兵共攻可突於。

translations.literal: The protector Xu Qindan led five hundred men of the prefecture’s armor together with the Xi chieftain Li Dapu’s troops to attack Ketuyu.
translations.idiomatic: The protector Xu Qindan led five hundred men of the prefecture’s armor together with the Xi chieftain Li Dapu’s troops against Ketuyu.

sentences.zh: 不勝，娑固、大酺皆死。

translations.literal: They did not prevail; Suogu and Dapu both died.
translations.idiomatic: They did not prevail. Suogu and Dapu both died.

sentences.zh: 欽澹懼，徙軍入榆關。

translations.literal: Qindan, in fear, moved his army into Yuguan.
translations.idiomatic: Qindan, in fear, withdrew his army into Yuguan.

sentences.zh: 可突於奉娑固從父弟郁于爲君，遣使者謝罪。

translations.literal: Ketuyu installed Suogu’s cousin on the father’s side, Yuyu, as ruler and sent envoys to apologize.
translations.idiomatic: Ketuyu set Suogu’s paternal cousin Yuyu on the throne and sent envoys to apologize.

sentences.zh: 有詔即拜郁於松漠郡王，而赦可突於。

translations.literal: There was an edict immediately enfeoffing Yuyu Prince of Songmo while pardoning Ketuyu.
translations.idiomatic: An edict at once enfeoffed Yuyu Prince of Songmo and pardoned Ketuyu.

sentences.zh: 郁於來朝，授率更令，以宗室所出女慕容爲燕郡公主妻之。

translations.literal: Yuyu came to court and was appointed Director of the Palace; a woman of the imperial clan named Murong was given as Princess of Yancheng to wife him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuyu came to court and was appointed Director of the Palace. A woman of the imperial clan named Murong was given as Princess of Yancheng to be his wife.

sentences.zh: 可突於亦來朝，擢左羽林衛將軍。

translations.literal: Ketuyu also came to court and was promoted Left Feathered Forest Guard General.
translations.idiomatic: Ketuyu also came to court and was made Left Feathered Forest Guard General.

sentences.zh: 郁于死，弟吐于嗣，與可突於有隙，不能定其下，攜公主來奔，封遼陽郡王，留宿衛。

translations.literal: When Yuyu died his younger brother Tuyu succeeded; he and Ketuyu were at odds and could not settle the people below; he brought the princess and came to submit, was enfeoffed Prince of Liaoyang, and remained in palace guard service.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuyu died his younger brother Tuyu succeeded. He and Ketuyu were at odds and could not hold the people below. He brought the princess and came to submit, was enfeoffed Prince of Liaoyang, and remained in palace guard service.

sentences.zh: 可突于奉盡忠弟邵固統衆，詔許襲王。

translations.literal: Ketuyu installed Jinzhong’s younger brother Shaogu to lead the multitude; an edict permitted him to inherit the princely title.
translations.idiomatic: Ketuyu installed Jinzhong’s younger brother Shaogu to lead the multitude, and an edict permitted him to inherit the princely title.

sentences.zh: 天子封禪，邵固與諸蕃長皆從行在。

translations.literal: When the Son of Heaven performed the Feng and Shan rites, Shaogu and the chieftains of the various tribes all followed the imperial progress.
translations.idiomatic: When the Son of Heaven performed the Feng and Shan rites, Shaogu and the chieftains of the various outer tribes all followed the imperial progress.

sentences.zh: 明年，拜左羽林衛大將軍，徙王廣化郡，以宗室出女陳爲東華公主，妻邵固，詔官其部酋長百餘人，邵固以子入侍。

translations.literal: The next year he was appointed Left Feathered Forest Guard Grand General, transferred to Prince of Guanghua, a woman of the imperial clan named Chen was given as Princess of Donghua to wife Shaogu, and an edict enfeoffed more than a hundred of his tribal chiefs; Shaogu sent his son in to serve at court.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was appointed Left Feathered Forest Guard Grand General and transferred to Prince of Guanghua. A woman of the imperial clan named Chen was given as Princess of Donghua to be Shaogu’s wife. An edict enfeoffed more than a hundred of his tribal chiefs, and Shaogu sent his son to serve at court.

sentences.zh: 可突於復來，不爲宰相李元紘所禮，鞅鞅去。

translations.literal: Ketuyu came again but was not treated with courtesy by the Chancellor Li Yuanhong and left discontented.
translations.idiomatic: Ketuyu came again but was not treated with courtesy by Chancellor Li Yuanhong and left discontented.

sentences.zh: 張說曰：「彼獸心者，唯利是向。

translations.literal: Zhang Yue said: "That one has a beast’s heart and looks only to profit."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yue said: "He has the heart of a beast and looks only to profit."

sentences.zh: 且方持國，下所附也，不假以禮，不來矣。

translations.literal: "Moreover he now holds a state; those below attach themselves to him. If you do not treat him with ritual, he will not come again."
translations.idiomatic: "Moreover he now holds a state, and those below attach themselves to him. If you do not treat him with ritual courtesy, he will not come again."

sentences.zh: 」後三年，可突于殺邵固，立屈烈爲王，脅奚衆共降突厥。

translations.literal: Three years later Ketuyu killed Shaogu, installed Qulie as king, and coerced the Xi multitude to submit together to the Turks.
translations.idiomatic: Three years later Ketuyu killed Shaogu, installed Qulie as king, and coerced the Xi multitude to submit with him to the Turks.

sentences.zh: 公主走平廬軍。

translations.literal: The princess fled to the Pinglu Army.
translations.idiomatic: The princess took refuge with the Pinglu Army.

sentences.zh: 詔幽州長史、知范陽節度事趙含章擊之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the Youzhou chief administrator and acting Fanyang frontier commissioner Zhao Hanzhang to strike them.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Youzhou chief administrator and acting Fanyang frontier commissioner Zhao Hanzhang to attack them.

sentences.zh: 遣中書舍人裴寬、給事中薛偘大募壯士，拜忠王浚河北道行軍元帥，以御史大夫李朝隱、京兆尹裴伷先副之，帥程伯獻、張文儼、宋之悌、李東蒙、趙萬功、郭英傑等八總管兵擊契丹。

translations.literal: The Palace Secretariat Drafter Pei Kuan and the Attendant of the Secretariat Pei Xun were sent to recruit stalwart men on a large scale; the Loyal Prince Jun was appointed grand marshal of the Hebei route army; the Censor-in-Chief Li Chaoyin and the Jingzhao Prefect Pei Youxian were his deputies; the commanders Cheng Boxian, Zhang Wenyian, Song Zhitui, Li Dongmeng, Zhao Wangong, Guo Yingjie, and others—eight route commanders in all—were to strike the Khitan.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Secretariat drafter Pei Kuan and Secretariat attendant Pei Xun were sent to recruit stalwart men on a large scale. The Loyal Prince Jun was appointed grand marshal of the Hebei route army, with Censor-in-Chief Li Chaoyin and Jingzhao prefect Pei Youxian as deputies. Commanders Cheng Boxian, Zhang Wenyian, Song Zhitui, Li Dongmeng, Zhao Wangong, Guo Yingjie, and others—eight route commanders in all—were to strike the Khitan.

sentences.zh: 既又以忠王兼河東道諸軍元帥，王不行。

translations.literal: Then the Loyal Prince was also made grand marshal of all armies of the Hedong route, but the prince did not go.
translations.idiomatic: The Loyal Prince was also made grand marshal of all armies on the Hedong route, but the prince did not go.

sentences.zh: 以禮部尚書信安郡王禕持節河北道行軍副元帥，與含章出塞捕虜，大破之。

translations.literal: The Minister of Rites Prince of Xin’an Li Yi was made deputy grand marshal with staff of authority on the Hebei route army; he and Hanzhang went beyond the frontier to capture the enemy and inflicted a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Rites Prince of Xin’an Li Yi was made deputy grand marshal with staff of authority on the Hebei route army. He and Hanzhang went beyond the frontier to capture the enemy and inflicted a great defeat.

sentences.zh: 可突于走，奚衆降，王以二蕃俘級告諸廟。

translations.literal: Ketuyu fled and the Xi multitude surrendered; the prince reported the heads of captives from the two tribes to the ancestral temples.
translations.idiomatic: Ketuyu fled and the Xi multitude surrendered. The prince reported the heads of captives from the two tribes to the ancestral temples.

sentences.zh: 明年，可突于盜邊，幽州長史薛楚玉、副總管郭英傑、吳克勤、烏知義、羅守忠率萬騎及奚擊之，戰都山下。

translations.literal: The next year Ketuyu raided the border; Youzhou chief administrator Xue Chuyu, deputy commanders Guo Yingjie, Wu Keqin, Wuzhiyi, and Luo Shouzhong led ten thousand horsemen together with the Xi to strike them and fought below Dushan.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Ketuyu raided the border. Youzhou chief administrator Xue Chuyu and deputy commanders Guo Yingjie, Wu Keqin, Wuzhiyi, and Luo Shouzhong led ten thousand horsemen together with the Xi against him and fought below Dushan.

sentences.zh: 可突於以突厥兵來，奚懼，持兩端，衆走險；

translations.literal: Ketuyu came with Türk troops; the Xi were afraid and held to both sides, and the multitude fled into difficult terrain;
translations.idiomatic: Ketuyu came with Türk troops. The Xi were afraid and wavered between two sides, and the multitude fled into difficult terrain.

sentences.zh: 知義、守忠敗，英傑、克勤死之，殺唐兵萬人。

translations.literal: Zhiyi and Shouzhong were defeated, Yingjie and Keqin died, and ten thousand Tang soldiers were killed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyi and Shouzhong were beaten. Yingjie and Keqin were killed, and ten thousand Tang soldiers died.

sentences.zh: 帝擢張守珪爲幽州長史經略之。

translations.literal: The Emperor promoted Zhang Shougui to Youzhou chief administrator to oversee the matter.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor promoted Zhang Shougui to Youzhou chief administrator to oversee the frontier.

sentences.zh: 守珪既善將，可突于恐，陽請臣而稍趨西北倚突厥。

translations.literal: Shougui being skilled as a commander, Ketuyu was afraid; he asked to submit in name while gradually leaning northwest to rely on the Turks.
translations.idiomatic: Shougui was a skilled commander, and Ketuyu was afraid. He asked to submit in name while gradually leaning northwest to rely on the Turks.

sentences.zh: 其衙官李過折與可突於內不平，守珪使客王悔陰邀之，以兵圍可突於，過折即夜斬可突于、屈烈及支黨數十人，自歸。

translations.literal: His yamen official Li Guozhe was inwardly at odds with Ketuyu; Shougui sent his retainer Wang Hui to invite him in secret; with troops he surrounded Ketuyu, and Guozhe by night cut off the heads of Ketuyu, Qulie, and several tens of their partisans and came to submit.
translations.idiomatic: His yamen official Li Guozhe was inwardly at odds with Ketuyu. Shougui sent his retainer Wang Hui to win him over in secret. With troops he surrounded Ketuyu, and Guozhe by night cut off the heads of Ketuyu, Qulie, and several tens of their partisans and came to submit.

sentences.zh: 守珪使過折統其部，函可突於等首傳東都。

translations.literal: Shougui had Guozhe lead his tribe and sent the heads of Ketuyu and the others boxed to the eastern capital.
translations.idiomatic: Shougui put Guozhe in charge of the tribe and sent Ketuyu’s head and the others boxed to the eastern capital.

sentences.zh: 拜過折北平郡王，爲松漠都督。

translations.literal: Guozhe was enfeoffed Prince of Beiping and made Songmo Protector.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhe was enfeoffed Prince of Beiping and made Songmo protector.

sentences.zh: 可突於殘黨擊殺過折，屠其家。

translations.literal: Ketuyu’s remnant partisans attacked and killed Guozhe and slaughtered his family.
translations.idiomatic: Ketuyu’s remnant followers killed Guozhe and slaughtered his household.

sentences.zh: 一子剌乾走安東，拜左驍衛將軍。

translations.literal: One son, Lagan, fled to Andong and was appointed Left Valiant Cavalry Guard General.
translations.idiomatic: One son, Lagan, fled to Andong and was appointed Left Valiant Cavalry Guard General.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，守珪討契丹，再破之，有詔自今戰有功必告廟。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year Shougui campaigned against the Khitan and defeated them again; there was an edict that from now on whenever there was merit in battle it must be reported to the temples.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year Shougui campaigned against the Khitan and defeated them again. An edict declared that from then on merit in battle must be reported to the temples.

sentences.zh: 天寶四載，契丹大酋李懷秀降，拜松漠都督，封崇順王，以宗室出女獨孤爲靜樂公主妻之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tianbao the great Khitan chief Li Huaijiu submitted and was appointed Songmo Protector, enfeoffed Prince of Chongshun; a woman of the imperial clan named Dugu was given as Princess of Jingle to wife him.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Tianbao the great Khitan chief Li Huaijiu submitted. He was appointed Songmo protector and enfeoffed Prince of Chongshun. A woman of the imperial clan named Dugu was given as Princess of Jingle to be his wife.

sentences.zh: 是歲，殺公主叛去，范陽節度使安祿山討破之。

translations.literal: That year he killed the princess and rebelled and fled; the Fanyang frontier commissioner An Lushan campaigned and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: That year he killed the princess, rebelled, and fled. The Fanyang frontier commissioner An Lushan campaigned against him and defeated him.

sentences.zh: 更封其酋楷落爲恭仁王，代松漠都督。

translations.literal: The chieftain Kailuo was further enfeoffed Prince of Gongren to replace the Songmo Protector.
translations.idiomatic: The chieftain Kailuo was further enfeoffed Prince of Gongren to replace him as Songmo protector.

sentences.zh: 祿山方幸，表討契丹以向帝意。

translations.literal: Lushan was then in favor and memorialized campaigning against the Khitan to suit the Emperor’s mind.
translations.idiomatic: Lushan was then in favor and memorialized a campaign against the Khitan to suit the emperor’s mind.

sentences.zh: 發幽州、雲中、平廬、河東兵十余萬，以奚爲鄉導，大戰潢水南。

translations.literal: He mobilized more than one hundred thousand troops from Youzhou, Yunzhong, Pinglu, and Hedong, with the Xi as guides, and fought a great battle south of the Huangshui.
translations.idiomatic: He raised more than one hundred thousand men from Youzhou, Yunzhong, Pinglu, and Hedong, used the Xi as guides, and fought a great battle south of the Huangshui.

sentences.zh: 祿山敗，死者數千。

translations.literal: Lushan was defeated and several thousand died.
translations.idiomatic: Lushan was defeated and several thousand men died.

sentences.zh: 自是祿山與相侵掠未嘗解，至其反乃已。

translations.literal: From then on Lushan and they raided and plundered each other without cease until his rebellion ended it.
translations.idiomatic: From then on Lushan and the Khitan raided each other without respite until his rebellion finally put an end to it.

sentences.zh: 契丹在開元、天寶間，使朝獻者無慮二十。

translations.literal: Between the Kaiyuan and Tianbao eras the Khitan sent tribute missions to court no fewer than twenty times.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaiyuan and Tianbao reigns the Khitan sent tribute missions to court at least twenty times.

sentences.zh: 故事，以范陽節度爲押奚、契丹使，自至德後，籓鎮擅地務自安，鄣戍斥候益謹，不生事于邊；

translations.literal: By precedent the Fanyang frontier commissioner served as commissioner for overseeing the Xi and Khitan; after the Zhide era the frontier commands held their territories and sought only their own security, frontier posts and scouts grew ever stricter, and they stirred no trouble on the border;
translations.idiomatic: By precedent the Fanyang commissioner also oversaw the Xi and Khitan. After the Zhide era the frontier commands held their own ground and sought only local security. Frontier posts and scouts grew stricter, and they stirred up no border trouble;

sentences.zh: 奚、契丹亦鮮入寇，歲選酋豪數十入長安朝會，每引見，賜與有秩，其下率數百皆駐館幽州。

translations.literal: the Xi and Khitan also rarely raided in; each year several tens of tribal chiefs were chosen to enter Chang’an for court assembly, and whenever they were received in audience gifts were bestowed in due rank; their followers, several hundred on average, all lodged at Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: the Xi and Khitan also rarely raided. Each year several dozen chiefs were chosen to attend court in Chang’an. Whenever they were received, gifts were bestowed in due rank, and their followers—several hundred on average—all lodged at Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 至德、寶應時再朝獻，大曆中十三，貞元間三，元和中七，大和、開成間凡四。

translations.literal: In the Zhide and Baoying eras they presented tribute twice; in the Dali era thirteen times; in the Zhenyuan era three; in the Yuanhe era seven; in the Dahe and Kaicheng eras four in all.
translations.idiomatic: They presented tribute twice in the Zhide and Baoying eras, thirteen times in Dali, three in Zhenyuan, seven in Yuanhe, and four in all during Dahe and Kaicheng.

sentences.zh: 然天子惡其外附回鶻，不復官爵渠長。

translations.literal: Yet the Son of Heaven disliked their attaching themselves to the Uyghurs and no longer enfeoffed or appointed their chieftains.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the Son of Heaven disliked their leaning on the Uyghurs and ceased to enfeoff or appoint their chieftains.

sentences.zh: 會昌二年，回鶻破，契丹酋屈戍始復內附，拜雲麾將軍、守右武衛將軍。

translations.literal: In the second year of Huichang, when the Uyghurs were broken, the Khitan chief Qu Shou first submitted within the borders again and was appointed Cloud-Banner General and Defender Right Martial Guard General.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Huichang, after the Uyghurs were broken, the Khitan chief Qu Shou submitted again and was appointed Cloud-Banner General and Defender Right Martial Guard General.

sentences.zh: 於是幽州節度使張仲武爲易回鶻所與舊印，賜唐新印，曰「奉國契丹之印」。

translations.literal: Then the Youzhou frontier commissioner Zhang Zhongwu had the old seal given by the Uyghurs exchanged and was granted a new Tang seal reading “Seal of the Khitan Who Serve the State.”
translations.idiomatic: The Youzhou frontier commissioner Zhang Zhongwu then had the old seal given by the Uyghurs exchanged for a new Tang seal reading “Seal of the Khitan Who Serve the State.”

sentences.zh: 咸通中，其王習爾之再遣使者入朝，部落浸強。

translations.literal: In the Xiantong era their king Xi’erzhi again sent envoys to court and the tribe gradually grew strong.
translations.idiomatic: In the Xiantong era their king Xi’erzhi again sent envoys to court, and the tribe gradually grew stronger.

sentences.zh: 習爾之死，族人欽德嗣。

translations.literal: When Xi’erzhi died, his clansman Qinde succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: When Xi’erzhi died, his clansman Qinde succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 光啟時，方天下盜興，北疆多故，乃鈔奚、室韋，小小部種皆役服之，因入寇幽、薊。

translations.literal: In the Guangqi era, when bandits rose throughout the realm and the northern frontier was beset, they plundered the Xi and Shiwei and made even the smallest tribal groups serve them, then raided You and Ji.
translations.idiomatic: In the Guangqi era, when bandits rose throughout the realm and the northern frontier was in turmoil, they plundered the Xi and Shiwei, brought even the smallest tribes under their sway, and raided You and Ji.

sentences.zh: 劉仁恭窮師逾摘星山討之，歲燎塞下草，使不得留牧，馬多死。

translations.literal: Liu Rengong exhausted his army crossing Zhaxing Mountain to campaign against them; each year he burned the grass below the frontier posts so they could not pasture, and many horses died.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Rengong exhausted his army crossing Zhaxing Mountain against them. Each year he burned the grass below the frontier posts so they could not pasture, and many of their horses died.

sentences.zh: 契丹乃乞盟，獻良馬求牧地，仁恭許之。

translations.literal: The Khitan then begged for alliance, presented fine horses, and sought pasture lands; Rengong granted it.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan then begged for alliance, presented fine horses, and sought pasture lands, and Rengong granted their request.

sentences.zh: 復敗約入寇，劉守光戍平州，契丹以萬騎入，守光偽與和，帳飲具於野，伏發，禽其大將。

translations.literal: They again broke the pact and raided in; Liu Shouguang garrisoned Pingzhou; the Khitan entered with ten thousand horsemen; Shouguang feigned peace and set out food and drink in the open camp, then sprang an ambush and captured their great general.
translations.idiomatic: They broke the pact again and raided. Liu Shouguang garrisoned Pingzhou when the Khitan entered with ten thousand horsemen. Shouguang feigned peace, set out food and drink in the open camp, sprang an ambush, and captured their great general.

sentences.zh: 群胡慟，願納馬五千以贖，不許。

translations.literal: The tribes were grief-stricken and wished to offer five thousand horses as ransom, but he would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: The tribes were grief-stricken and offered five thousand horses as ransom, but he would not accept.

sentences.zh: 欽德輸重賂求之，乃與盟，十年不敢近邊。

translations.literal: Qinde paid heavy bribes to seek his release, and they then made alliance and for ten years did not dare approach the border.
translations.idiomatic: Qinde paid heavy bribes to ransom him. They then made alliance, and for ten years did not dare approach the border.

sentences.zh: 欽德晚節政不競，其八部大人法常三歲代，時耶律阿保機建鼓旗爲一部，不肯代，自號爲王而有國，大賀氏遂亡。

translations.literal: In Qinde’s later years his government could not compete; the great men of the eight tribes by law replaced one another every three years, but at that time Yelü Abaoji raised drums and banners as one tribe and would not step down, styled himself king and had a state, and the Dahe clan then perished.
translations.idiomatic: In Qinde’s later years his rule could not hold. The great men of the eight tribes were by law replaced every three years, but Yelü Abaoji raised drums and banners as one tribe, refused to step down, styled himself king and founded a state, and the Dahe clan then perished.

sentences.zh: 奚，亦東胡種，爲匈奴所破，保烏丸山。

translations.literal: The Xi were also of Eastern Hu stock; broken by the Xiongnu, they held to Wuyan Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: The Xi were also an Eastern Hu people. Broken by the Xiongnu, they held to Wuyan Mountain.

sentences.zh: 漢曹操斬其帥蹋頓，蓋其後也。

translations.literal: In Han, Cao Cao beheaded their chief Tadun— they were his descendants.
translations.idiomatic: In Han times Cao Cao beheaded their chief Tadun; they were his descendants.

sentences.zh: 元魏時自號庫真奚，居鮮卑故地，直京師東北四千里。

translations.literal: In the Northern Wei era they styled themselves Kuzhen Xi and dwelt in the old Xianbei lands, straight northeast of the capital four thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Northern Wei they styled themselves Kuzhen Xi and dwelt in the old Xianbei lands, some four thousand li northeast of the capital.

sentences.zh: 其地東北接契丹，西突厥，南白狼河，北霫。

translations.literal: Their territory bordered the Khitan on the northeast, the Turks on the west, the Bailang River on the south, and the Mohe on the north.
translations.idiomatic: Their lands bordered the Khitan on the northeast, the Turks on the west, the Bailang River on the south, and the Mohe on the north.

sentences.zh: 與突厥同俗，逐水草畜牧，居氈廬，環車爲營。

translations.literal: Their customs were the same as the Turks’; they followed water and grass to pasture livestock, lived in felt yurts, and ringed carts to make camps.
translations.idiomatic: Their customs matched the Turks’. They followed water and grass with their herds, lived in felt yurts, and ringed their carts to make camps.

sentences.zh: 其君長常以五百人持兵衛牙中，餘部散山谷間，無賦入，以射獵爲貲。

translations.literal: Their chieftain constantly kept five hundred men bearing arms to guard the headquarters; the rest of the tribes were scattered in mountain valleys with no tax levies, taking hunting as their wealth.
translations.idiomatic: Their chieftain constantly kept five hundred armed men at his headquarters. The rest of the tribes were scattered through mountain valleys, paid no taxes, and lived by the hunt.

sentences.zh: 稼多穄，已獲，窖山下。

translations.literal: They mostly planted millet; once harvested they stored it in pits in the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: They mostly planted millet. Once harvested, they stored it in pits in the mountains.

sentences.zh: 斷木爲臼，瓦鼎爲飦，雜寒水而食。

translations.literal: They split wood for mortars and used earthen pots for gruel, mixing in cold water to eat.
translations.idiomatic: They split wood for mortars, cooked gruel in earthen pots, and mixed in cold water to eat.

sentences.zh: 喜戰鬥，兵有五部，部一俟斤主之。

translations.literal: They delighted in fighting; the army had five divisions, each division ruled by one irkin.
translations.idiomatic: They delighted in fighting. Their forces had five divisions, each ruled by an irkin.

sentences.zh: 其國西抵大洛泊，距回紇牙三千里，多依土護真水。

translations.literal: Their state reached west to Great Luobo Marsh, three thousand li from the Uyghur headquarters, and mostly relied on the Tuhu River.
translations.idiomatic: Their state reached west to Great Luobo Marsh, three thousand li from the Uyghur headquarters, and for the most part lived along the Tuhu River.

sentences.zh: 其馬善登，其羊黑。

translations.literal: Their horses were good at climbing and their sheep black.
translations.idiomatic: Their horses were sure-footed climbers and their sheep black.

sentences.zh: 盛夏必徙保冷陘山，山直媯州西北。

translations.literal: In high summer they always moved to hold Lengxing Mountain, which lay northwest of Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In high summer they always withdrew to Lengxing Mountain, northwest of Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 至隋始去「庫真」，但曰奚。

translations.literal: Reaching Sui they dropped “Kuzhen” and were called only Xi.
translations.idiomatic: In Sui times they dropped “Kuzhen” and were called simply Xi.

sentences.zh: 武德中，高開道借其兵再寇幽州，長史王詵擊破之。

translations.literal: In the Wude era Gao Kaidao twice borrowed their troops to raid Youzhou and was defeated by Chief Administrator Wang Shen.
translations.idiomatic: In the Wude era Gao Kaidao twice borrowed their troops to raid Youzhou and was beaten by Chief Administrator Wang Shen.

sentences.zh: 太宗貞觀三年始來朝，閱十七歲，凡四朝貢。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhenguan of Taizong they first came to court; over seventeen years they presented tribute four times.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Zhenguan they first came to court. Over the next seventeen years they presented tribute four times.

sentences.zh: 帝伐高麗，大酋蘇支從戰有功。

translations.literal: When the Emperor campaigned against Goguryeo, the great chief Suzhi followed the army and had merit.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor campaigned against Goguryeo, the great chief Suzhi followed the army and won merit.

sentences.zh: 不數年，其長可度者內附，帝爲置饒樂都督府，拜可度者使持節六州諸軍事、饒樂都督，封樓煩縣公，賜李氏。

translations.literal: Within a few years their chief Keduzhe submitted within the borders; the Emperor established the Raole Protectorate, appointed Keduzhe commissioner with staff of authority over the military affairs of six prefectures and Raole Protector, enfeoffed him Duke of Loufan, and granted the surname Li.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few years their chief Keduzhe submitted. The emperor established the Raole Protectorate, made Keduzhe commissioner with staff of authority over six prefectures’ military affairs and Raole protector, enfeoffed him Duke of Loufan, and granted the surname Li.

sentences.zh: 以阿會部爲弱水州，處和部爲祁黎州，奧失部爲洛瑰州，度稽部爲太魯州，元俟折部爲渴野州，各以酋領辱紇主爲刺史，隸饒樂府。

translations.literal: The Ahui tribe was made Ruoshui Prefecture, the Chuhe tribe Qili Prefecture, the Aoshi tribe Luogui Prefecture, the Duji tribe Tailu Prefecture, the Yuanhouzhe tribe Keye Prefecture—each with its tribal chief Ruhuo Zhuzhu as prefect, all subordinate to Raole.
translations.idiomatic: The Ahui tribe became Ruoshui Prefecture, the Chuhe Qili, the Aoshi Luogui, the Duji Tailu, and the Yuanhouzhe Keye—each with its tribal chief Ruhuo Zhuzhu as prefect, all under Raole.

sentences.zh: 復置東夷都護府于營州，兼統松漠、饒樂地，置東夷校尉。

translations.literal: The Eastern Yi Protectorate was restored at Yingzhou, jointly overseeing Songmo and Raole lands, with an Eastern Yi adjutant set.
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Yi Protectorate was restored at Yingzhou to oversee Songmo and Raole together, with an Eastern Yi adjutant appointed.

sentences.zh: 顯慶間可度者死，奚遂叛。

translations.literal: In the Xianqing era Keduzhe died and the Xi then rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: In the Xianqing era Keduzhe died, and the Xi rebelled.

sentences.zh: 五年，以定襄都督阿史德樞賓、左武候將軍延陀梯真、居延州都督李含珠爲冷陘道行軍總管。

translations.literal: In the fifth year Ashide Shubin, Dingxiang Protector, Yan Tizhen, Left Martial Guard General, and Li Hanzhu, Juyan Protector, were made commanders of the Lengxing route army.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year Ashide Shubin, Dingxiang protector, Yan Tizhen, Left Martial Guard general, and Li Hanzhu, Juyan protector, were made commanders of the Lengxing route army.

sentences.zh: 明年，詔尚書右丞崔餘慶持節總護定襄等三都督討之，奚懼乞降，斬其王匹帝。

translations.literal: The next year an edict made Vice Director of the Secretariat Cui Yuqing commissioner with staff of authority to oversee the three Dingxiang protectors in punishing them; the Xi were afraid and begged to surrender, beheading their king Pidi.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Vice Director of the Secretariat Cui Yuqing was ordered to oversee the three Dingxiang protectors in punishing them. The Xi were afraid and begged to surrender, beheading their king Pidi.

sentences.zh: 萬歲通天中，契丹反，奚亦叛，與突厥相表裏，號「兩蕃」。

translations.literal: In the Wansui Tongtian era the Khitan rebelled and the Xi rebelled too, acting in concert with the Turks and styled the “Two Tribes.”
translations.idiomatic: In the Wansui Tongtian era the Khitan rebelled and the Xi rebelled with them, acting in concert with the Turks and styled the “Two Tribes.”

sentences.zh: 延和元年，以左羽林衛大將軍幽州都督孫佺、左驍衛將軍李楷洛、左威衛將軍周以悌帥兵十二萬，爲三軍，襲擊其部。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yanhe the Left Feathered Forest Guard Grand General and Youzhou Protector Sun Quan, Left Valiant Cavalry Guard General Li Kailuo, and Left Martial Guard General Zhou Yiti led one hundred twenty thousand troops in three armies to strike their tribes.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yanhe the Left Feathered Forest Guard Grand General and Youzhou Protector Sun Quan, Left Valiant Cavalry Guard General Li Kailuo, and Left Martial Guard General Zhou Yiti led one hundred twenty thousand men in three armies against their tribes.

sentences.zh: 次冷陘，前軍楷洛與奚酋李大酺戰不利。

translations.literal: They halted at Lengxing; the vanguard Kailuo fought the Xi chief Li Dapu and fared poorly.
translations.idiomatic: They halted at Lengxing. The vanguard Kailuo fought the Xi chief Li Dapu and fared poorly.

sentences.zh: 佺懼，斂軍，詐大酺曰：「我奉詔來慰撫若等，而楷洛違節度輒戰，非天子意，方戮以徇。

translations.literal: Quan was afraid and drew in the army, falsely telling Dapu: “I have come by edict to comfort you, yet Kailuo disobeyed the command and fought—this is not the Son of Heaven’s intent; I am about to execute him as a warning.”
translations.idiomatic: Quan was afraid and drew in his army. He falsely told Dapu: “I came by edict to comfort you, yet Kailuo disobeyed the command and fought—this is not the Son of Heaven’s intent. I am about to execute him as a warning.”

sentences.zh: 」大酺曰：「誠慰撫我，有所賜乎？

translations.literal: Dapu said: “If you truly comfort us, is there something you will grant?”
translations.idiomatic: Dapu said: “If you truly mean to comfort us, will you grant us something?”

sentences.zh: 」佺出軍中繒帛、袍帶與之。

translations.literal: Quan brought out silks, robes, and belts from the army and gave them to him.
translations.idiomatic: Quan brought out silks, robes, and belts from the army stores and gave them to him.

sentences.zh: 大酺謝，請佺還師，舉軍得脫，爭先無部伍，大酺兵躡之，遂大敗，殺傷數萬。

translations.literal: Dapu thanked him and asked Quan to withdraw the army; the whole force escaped, scrambling ahead without formation, and Dapu’s troops pursued them and they were utterly defeated, tens of thousands killed and wounded.
translations.idiomatic: Dapu thanked him and asked Quan to withdraw. The whole force escaped, scrambling ahead without formation. Dapu’s troops pursued and routed them, killing and wounding tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 佺、以悌皆爲虜禽，送默啜害之。

translations.literal: Quan and Yiti were both captured and sent to Mojie, who killed them.
translations.idiomatic: Quan and Yiti were both taken captive and sent to Mojie, who put them to death.

sentences.zh: 朝廷方多故，不暇討。

translations.literal: The court was then beset with many troubles and had no leisure to punish them.
translations.idiomatic: The court was then overwhelmed with troubles and had no leisure to punish them.

sentences.zh: 玄宗開元二年，使奧蘇悔落丐降，封饒樂郡王，左金吾衛大將軍、饒樂都督。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kaiyuan of Xuanzong, Aosuhuila came to beg surrender and was enfeoffed Prince of Raole, Left Golden Guard Grand General, and Raole Protector.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Kaiyuan, Aosuhuila came to beg surrender and was enfeoffed Prince of Raole, Left Golden Guard Grand General, and Raole protector.

sentences.zh: 詔宗室出女辛爲固安公主，妻大酺。

translations.literal: An edict gave a woman of the imperial clan named Xin as Princess of Guo’an to wife Dapu.
translations.idiomatic: An edict gave a woman of the imperial clan named Xin as Princess of Guo’an to be Dapu’s wife.

sentences.zh: 明年，身入朝成昏。

translations.literal: The next year he came in person to court to complete the marriage.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he came in person to court to complete the marriage.

sentences.zh: 始復營州都督府，遣右領軍將軍李濟持節護送。

translations.literal: The Yingzhou Protectorate was first restored and the Right Leading Guard General Li Ji was sent with staff of authority to escort him.
translations.idiomatic: The Yingzhou Protectorate was restored, and Right Leading Guard General Li Ji was sent with staff of authority to escort him.

sentences.zh: 大酺後與契丹可突於鬥，死。

translations.literal: Later Dapu fought Ketuyu of the Khitan and died.
translations.idiomatic: Later Dapu fought the Khitan Ketuyu and died.

sentences.zh: 弟魯蘇領其部，襲王。

translations.literal: His younger brother Lusu took his tribe and inherited the princely title.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Lusu took over the tribe and inherited the princely title.

sentences.zh: 詔兼保塞軍經略大使。

translations.literal: An edict made him also frontier commissioner of the Baosai Army.
translations.idiomatic: An edict also made him frontier commissioner of the Baosai Army.

sentences.zh: 牙官塞默羯謀叛，公主置酒誘殺之，帝嘉其功，賜主累萬。

translations.literal: His yamen official Sai Mojie plotted rebellion; the princess set out wine and lured him to his death; the Emperor praised her merit and bestowed on the princess tens of thousands in gifts.
translations.idiomatic: His yamen official Sai Mojie plotted rebellion. The princess set out wine and lured him to his death. The emperor praised her merit and bestowed tens of thousands in gifts on the princess.

sentences.zh: 會與其母相告訐得罪，更以盛安公主女韋爲東光公主妻之。

translations.literal: When she and her mother mutually accused each other they were found guilty; another woman of the imperial clan, the Princess of Sheng’an’s daughter Wei, was given as Princess of Dongguang to wife him.
translations.idiomatic: When she and her mother mutually accused each other they were found guilty. Another woman of the imperial clan—the Princess of Sheng’an’s daughter Wei—was given as Princess of Dongguang to be his wife.

sentences.zh: 後三年，封魯蘇奉誠郡王，右羽林衛將軍，擢其首領無慮二百人，皆位郎將。

translations.literal: Three years later Lusu was enfeoffed Prince of Fengcheng, Right Feathered Forest Guard General, and more than two hundred of his chiefs were promoted—all to Gentleman of the Palace Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Three years later Lusu was enfeoffed Prince of Fengcheng and Right Feathered Forest Guard General, and more than two hundred of his chiefs were promoted—all to gentlemen of the palace guard.

sentences.zh: 久之，契丹可突於反，脅奚衆並附突厥。

translations.literal: Before long the Khitan Ketuyu rebelled and coerced the Xi multitude to submit together to the Turks.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Khitan Ketuyu rebelled and coerced the Xi multitude to submit with him to the Turks.

sentences.zh: 魯蘇不能制，奔榆關，公主奔平廬。

translations.literal: Lusu could not control them and fled to Yuguan; the princess fled to the Pinglu Army.
translations.idiomatic: Lusu could not control them and fled to Yuguan. The princess fled to the Pinglu Army.

sentences.zh: 幽州長史趙含章發清夷軍討破之，衆稍自歸。

translations.literal: Youzhou Chief Administrator Zhao Hanzhang mobilized the Qingyi Army to strike and defeat them, and the multitude gradually returned on their own.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhou chief administrator Zhao Hanzhang mobilized the Qingyi Army, struck them, and defeated them. The people gradually returned on their own.

sentences.zh: 明年，信安王禕降其酋李詩鎖高等部落五千帳，以其地爲歸義州，因以王詩，拜左羽林軍大將軍、本州都督，賜帛十萬，置其部幽州之偏。

translations.literal: The next year Prince of Xin’an Li Yi received the surrender of the chiefs Li Shisuo and Gao and their tribes of five thousand tents; their lands were made Guiyi Prefecture; Shisuo was enfeoffed, appointed Left Feathered Forest Army Grand General and prefect of the prefecture, granted one hundred thousand bolts of silk, and his tribe was placed on the outskirts of Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Prince of Xin’an Li Yi received the surrender of the chiefs Li Shisuo and Gao and five thousand tents of their tribes. Their lands were made Guiyi Prefecture. Shisuo was enfeoffed, appointed Left Feathered Forest Army Grand General and prefect, granted one hundred thousand bolts of silk, and his tribe was settled on the outskirts of Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 李詩死，子延寵嗣，與契丹又叛，爲幽州張守珪所困。

translations.literal: When Shisuo died his son Yanchong succeeded; he rebelled again together with the Khitan and was hemmed in by Zhang Shougui of Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Shisuo died his son Yanchong succeeded. He rebelled again with the Khitan and was hemmed in by Zhang Shougui of Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 延寵降，復拜饒樂都督、懷信王，以宗室出女楊爲宜芳公主妻之。

translations.literal: Yanchong surrendered and was again appointed Raole Protector and Prince of Huaixin; a woman of the imperial clan named Yang was given as Princess of Yifang to wife him.
translations.idiomatic: Yanchong surrendered and was again made Raole protector and Prince of Huaixin. A woman of the imperial clan named Yang was given as Princess of Yifang to be his wife.

sentences.zh: 延寵殺公主復叛，詔立它酋婆固爲昭信王、饒樂都督，以定其部。

translations.literal: Yanchong killed the princess and rebelled again; an edict installed another chief Pogu as Prince of Zhaoxin and Raole Protector to settle the tribe.
translations.idiomatic: Yanchong killed the princess and rebelled again. An edict installed another chief Pogu as Prince of Zhaoxin and Raole protector to settle the tribe.

sentences.zh: 安祿山節度范陽，詭邊功，數與鏖鬥，飾俘以獻，誅其君李日越，料所俘驍壯戍雲南。

translations.literal: An Lushan held Fanyang and fabricated frontier merit, repeatedly clashing with them, dressing captives to present, executing their chief Li Riyue, and assigning the captured stalwarts to garrison Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: An Lushan held Fanyang, fabricated frontier merit, and repeatedly clashed with them. He dressed captives for presentation, executed their chief Li Riyue, and sent the captured stalwarts to garrison Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 終帝世，凡八朝獻，至德、大曆間十二。

translations.literal: Through the whole of the Emperor’s reign they presented tribute eight times; in the Zhide and Dali eras twelve.
translations.idiomatic: Through the whole of the emperor’s reign they presented tribute eight times; in the Zhide and Dali eras, twelve.

sentences.zh: 是後契丹方強，奚不敢亢，而舉部役屬。

translations.literal: After that the Khitan were strong and the Xi did not dare contend but had their whole tribe made to serve.
translations.idiomatic: After that the Khitan grew strong and the Xi did not dare contend but had their whole tribe made to serve them.

sentences.zh: 虜政苛，奚怨之，其酋去諸引別部內附，保媯州北山，遂爲東、西奚。

translations.literal: Barbarian rule was harsh and the Xi resented it; their chief Quzhu led a separate tribe to submit within the borders, holding the mountains north of Guizhou, and thus there came Eastern and Western Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Barbarian rule was harsh and the Xi resented it. Their chief Quzhu led a separate tribe to submit, holding the mountains north of Guizhou, and thus there came Eastern and Western Xi.

sentences.zh: 室韋，契丹別種，東胡之北邊，蓋丁零苗裔也。

translations.literal: The Shiwei were a separate branch of the Khitan, the northern borderland of the Eastern Hu— in origin probably descendants of the Dingling.
translations.idiomatic: The Shiwei were a separate branch of the Khitan on the northern borderland of the Eastern Hu—in origin probably descendants of the Dingling.

sentences.zh: 地據黃龍北，傍峱越河，直京師東北七千里，東黑水靺鞨，西突厥，南契丹，北瀕海。

translations.literal: Their lands lay north of Huanglong beside the Naoyue River, straight northeast of the capital seven thousand li, east bordering the Heishui Mohe, west the Turks, south the Khitan, north the sea.
translations.idiomatic: Their lands lay north of Huanglong beside the Naoyue River, some seven thousand li northeast of the capital, bordering the Heishui Mohe on the east, the Turks on the west, the Khitan on the south, and the sea on the north.

sentences.zh: 其國無君長，惟大酋，皆號「莫賀咄」，攝筦其部而附於突厥。

translations.literal: Their state had no single ruler but only great chiefs, all styled “Mohuduo,” who governed their tribes and submitted to the Turks.
translations.idiomatic: Their state had no single ruler, only great chiefs all styled “Mohuduo,” who governed their tribes and submitted to the Turks.

sentences.zh: 小或千戶，大數千戶，濱散川穀，逐水草而處，不稅斂。

translations.literal: The small might have a thousand households, the large several thousand; they were scattered along streams and valleys, following water and grass, with no taxation.
translations.idiomatic: Small groups might have a thousand households, large ones several thousand. They were scattered along streams and valleys, following water and grass, with no taxation.

sentences.zh: 每弋獵即相嘯聚，事畢去，不相臣制，故雖猛悍喜戰，而卒不能爲強國。

translations.literal: Whenever they went hunting they would gather with a shout; when the affair was done they dispersed and did not subject one another—thus though fierce and fond of war they could in the end not become a strong state.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever they hunted they gathered with a shout and dispersed when done, subject to no one. Thus though fierce and fond of war, they could never become a strong state.

sentences.zh: 剡木爲犁，人挽以耕，田獲甚褊。

translations.literal: They carved wood for plows and men pulled them to till; the harvest was very meager.
translations.idiomatic: They carved wood for plows and men pulled them to till. The harvest was very meager.

sentences.zh: 其氣候多寒，夏霧雨，冬霜霰。

translations.literal: Their climate was mostly cold; in summer fog and rain, in winter frost and hail.
translations.idiomatic: Their climate was mostly cold—fog and rain in summer, frost and hail in winter.

sentences.zh: 其俗，富人以五色珠垂領，婚嫁則男先傭女家三歲，而後分以產，與婦共載，鼓舞而還。

translations.literal: By custom the rich hung colored beads at the collar; for marriage the man first served the woman’s family three years, then they divided property and rode back together with the wife, drumming and dancing.
translations.idiomatic: By custom the rich hung colored beads at the collar. For marriage the man first served the woman’s family three years; then they divided property and rode back together with drumming and dancing.

sentences.zh: 夫死，不再嫁。

translations.literal: When the husband died she did not remarry.
translations.idiomatic: If her husband died, she did not marry again.

sentences.zh: 每部共構大棚，死者置屍其上，喪期三年。

translations.literal: Each tribe jointly built a great lodge and placed the corpse atop it; the mourning period was three years.
translations.idiomatic: Each tribe jointly built a great lodge and placed the corpse atop it. The mourning period was three years.

sentences.zh: 土少金鐵，率資於高麗。

translations.literal: Their land had little gold or iron and they mostly obtained it from Goguryeo.
translations.idiomatic: Their land had little gold or iron, and they mostly obtained it from Goguryeo.

sentences.zh: 器有角弓、楛矢，人尤善射。

translations.literal: Their weapons included horn bows and wooden arrows; the people were especially skilled at shooting.
translations.idiomatic: Their weapons included horn bows and wooden arrows, and the people were especially skilled at shooting.

sentences.zh: 每溽夏，西保貣勃、次對二山。

translations.literal: Each sultry summer they withdrew west to hold the two mountains Zhibo and Cidui.
translations.idiomatic: Every sultry summer they withdrew west to hold the two mountains Zhibo and Cidui.

sentences.zh: 山多草木鳥獸，然苦飛蚊，則巢居以避。

translations.literal: The mountains had much grass, trees, birds, and beasts, but they suffered from flying mosquitoes and therefore nested in trees to avoid them.
translations.idiomatic: The mountains had much grass, trees, birds, and beasts, but flying mosquitoes tormented them, so they nested in trees to escape.

sentences.zh: 酋帥死，以子弟繼，無則推豪桀立之。

translations.literal: When a chieftain died a younger kinsman succeeded; if none, a powerful man was pushed forward to stand.
translations.idiomatic: When a chieftain died a younger kinsman succeeded; if none, a powerful man was pushed forward to rule.

sentences.zh: 率乘牛車，蘧蒢爲室，度水則束薪爲桴，或以皮爲舟。

translations.literal: They mostly rode ox carts, used rushes for dwellings, bound firewood into rafts to cross water, or sometimes made boats of hide.
translations.idiomatic: They mostly rode ox carts and used rushes for dwellings. To cross water they bound firewood into rafts or sometimes made boats of hide.

sentences.zh: 馬皆草韉、繩羈靮。

translations.literal: Horses all had grass saddles and rope bridles and reins.
translations.idiomatic: Their horses all had grass saddles and rope bridles and reins.

sentences.zh: 所居或皮蒙室，或屈木以蘧蒢覆，徙則載而行。

translations.literal: Where they dwelt was sometimes a lodge skin-covered, sometimes bent wood covered with rushes; when they moved they loaded and went.
translations.idiomatic: Where they dwelt was sometimes skin-covered lodges, sometimes bent wood covered with rushes. When they moved they loaded everything and went.

sentences.zh: 其畜無羊少馬，有牛不用，有巨豕食之，韋其皮爲服若席。

translations.literal: Of livestock they had no sheep and few horses, had cattle but did not use them, had huge swine for food, and tanned their hides for clothing or mats.
translations.idiomatic: They had no sheep and few horses, had cattle but did not use them, kept huge swine for food, and tanned their hides for clothing or mats.

sentences.zh: 其語言，靺鞨也。

translations.literal: Their language was that of the Mohe.
translations.idiomatic: They spoke the language of the Mohe.

sentences.zh: 分部凡二十餘：曰嶺西部、山北部、黃頭部，強部也；

translations.literal: The divisions numbered more than twenty: the Lingxi tribe, the Shanbei tribe, and the Huangtou tribe were strong tribes;
translations.idiomatic: Their divisions numbered more than twenty. The Lingxi tribe, the Shanbei tribe, and the Huangtou tribe were the strong ones;

sentences.zh: 大如者部、小如者部、婆萵部、訥北部、駱丹部，悉處柳城東北，近者三千，遠六千里而贏；

translations.literal: the Daruzhe tribe, the Xiaoruzhe tribe, the Powo tribe, the Nebei tribe, and the Luodan tribe—all dwelt northeast of Liucheng, the near three thousand li, the far more than six thousand li;
translations.idiomatic: the Daruzhe, Xiaoruzhe, Powo, Nebei, and Luodan tribes—all dwelt northeast of Liucheng, the near at three thousand li, the far more than six thousand;

sentences.zh: 最西有烏素固部，與回紇接，當俱倫泊之西南；

translations.literal: farthest west was the Wusugu tribe, adjoining the Uyghurs, facing the southwest of Julun Marsh;
translations.idiomatic: farthest west was the Wusugu tribe, adjoining the Uyghurs on the southwest of Julun Marsh;

sentences.zh: 自泊而東有移塞沒部；

translations.literal: east of the marsh was the Yisaimo tribe;
translations.idiomatic: East of the marsh lay the Yisaimo tribe;

sentences.zh: 稍東有塞曷支部，最強部也，居啜河之陰，亦曰燕支河；

translations.literal: farther east was the Saihe tribe, the strongest tribe, dwelling on the north bank of the Chuo River, also called the Yanzhi River;
translations.idiomatic: farther east was the Saihe tribe, the strongest, dwelling on the north bank of the Chuo River, also called the Yanzhi River;

sentences.zh: 益東有和解部、烏羅護部、那禮部、嶺西部；

translations.literal: still farther east were the Hejie tribe, the Wuluohu tribe, the Nali tribe, and the Lingxi tribe;
translations.idiomatic: still farther east were the Hejie, Wuluohu, Nali, and Lingxi tribes;

sentences.zh: 直北曰訥比支部，北有大山，山外曰大室韋，瀕於室建河，河出俱倫，迆而東；

translations.literal: due north was the Nebi tribe; north was a great mountain, and beyond the mountain Great Shiwei, bordering the Shijian River, which issued from Julun and wound east;
translations.idiomatic: due north was the Nebi tribe. North was a great mountain, and beyond it Great Shiwei, bordering the Shijian River, which issued from Julun and wound east;

sentences.zh: 河南有蒙瓦部，其北落坦部；

translations.literal: south of the river were the Mengwa tribe and the Beiluo Tan tribe;
translations.idiomatic: South of the river were the Mengwa and Beiluo Tan tribes;

sentences.zh: 水東合那河、忽汗河，又東貫黑水靺鞨，故靺鞨跨水有南北部，而東注於海。

translations.literal: east of the water the Na River and Hohan River joined, and farther east pierced the Heishui Mohe—thus the Mohe straddled the water with north and south divisions and flowed east into the sea.
translations.idiomatic: east of the water the Na River and Hohan River joined, and farther east pierced the Heishui Mohe. Thus the Mohe straddled the water with north and south divisions and flowed east into the sea.

sentences.zh: 峱越河東南亦與那河合，其北有東室韋，蓋烏丸東南鄙餘人也。

translations.literal: Southeast of the Naoyue River it also joined the Na River; to its north was Eastern Shiwei, probably the remnant people of Wuyan’s southeastern borderland.
translations.idiomatic: Southeast of the Naoyue River it also joined the Na River. To its north was Eastern Shiwei, probably the remnant people of Wuyan’s southeastern borderland.

sentences.zh: 貞觀五年，始來貢豐貂，後再入朝。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Zhenguan they first presented tribute of rich sable; later they came to court again.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Zhenguan they first presented rich sable as tribute; later they came to court again.

sentences.zh: 長壽二年叛，將軍李多祚擊定之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Changshou they rebelled and General Li Duozuo struck and settled them.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Changshou they rebelled, and General Li Duozuo struck and settled them.

sentences.zh: 景龍初，復朝獻，請助討突厥。

translations.literal: In the beginning of Jinglong they again presented tribute and asked to help punish the Turks.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Jinglong they again presented tribute and asked to help punish the Turks.

sentences.zh: 開元、天寶間，凡十朝獻，大曆中十一。

translations.literal: Between Kaiyuan and Tianbao they presented tribute ten times in all; in the Dali era eleven.
translations.idiomatic: Between Kaiyuan and Tianbao they presented tribute ten times in all; in the Dali era, eleven.

sentences.zh: 貞元四年，與奚共寇振武，節度使唐朝臣方郊勞天子使者，驚而走軍，室韋執詔使，大殺掠而去。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhenyuan they raided Zhenwu together with the Xi; Frontier Commissioner Tang Chaochen was in the suburbs receiving the Son of Heaven’s envoy when startled he fled with the army; the Shiwei seized the edict-bearer and departed after great slaughter and plunder.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Zhenyuan they raided Zhenwu together with the Xi. Frontier Commissioner Tang Chaochen was receiving the Son of Heaven’s envoy in the suburbs when startled he fled with his army. The Shiwei seized the edict-bearer and departed after great slaughter and plunder.

sentences.zh: 明年，使者來謝。

translations.literal: The next year envoys came to apologize.
translations.idiomatic: The next year their envoys came to apologize.

sentences.zh: 大和中三朝獻。

translations.literal: In the Dahe era they presented tribute three times.
translations.idiomatic: During the Dahe era they presented tribute on three occasions.

sentences.zh: 大中中一來。

translations.literal: In the Dazhong era they came once.
translations.idiomatic: In the Dazhong era they came once.

sentences.zh: 咸通時，大酋怛烈與奚皆遣使至京師，然非顯夷後，史官失傳。

translations.literal: In the Xiantong era the great chief Dilie and the Xi all sent envoys to the capital, but they were not descendants of illustrious barbarians and the historiographers lost the record.
translations.idiomatic: In the Xiantong era the great chief Dilie and the Xi all sent envoys to the capital, but they were not descendants of illustrious barbarians, and the historiographers lost the record.

sentences.zh: 黑水靺鞨居肅慎地，亦曰挹婁，元魏時曰勿吉。

translations.literal: The Heishui Mohe dwelt in the Sushhen lands, also called Yilou; in the Northern Wei era called Wuji.
translations.idiomatic: The Heishui Mohe dwelt in the Sushhen lands, also called Yilou; in the Northern Wei era they were called Wuji.

sentences.zh: 直京師東北六千里，東瀕海，西屬突厥，南高麗，北室韋。

translations.literal: Straight northeast of the capital six thousand li, east bordering the sea, west subject to the Turks, south Goguryeo, north the Shiwei.
translations.idiomatic: Their lands lay some six thousand li northeast of the capital, bordering the sea on the east, subject to the Turks on the west, Goguryeo on the south, and the Shiwei on the north.

sentences.zh: 離爲數十部，酋各自治。

translations.literal: They were divided into several tens of tribes, each chief governing on his own.
translations.idiomatic: They were divided into several dozen tribes, each chief governing on his own.

sentences.zh: 其著者曰粟末部，居最南，抵太白山，亦曰徒太山，與高麗接，依粟末水以居，水源於山西，北注它漏河；

translations.literal: The prominent one was called the Sumo tribe, dwelling farthest south, reaching Great White Mountain, also called Taitai Mountain, adjoining Goguryeo and dwelling by the Sumo River; the river issued from the west of the mountain and flowed north into the Talou River;
translations.idiomatic: The prominent tribe was the Sumo, dwelling farthest south at Great White Mountain, also called Taitai Mountain, adjoining Goguryeo and living by the Sumo River. The river issued from the west of the mountain and flowed north into the Talou River;

sentences.zh: 稍東北曰汨咄部；

translations.literal: somewhat northeast was the Mizhu tribe;
translations.idiomatic: somewhat to the northeast was the Mizhu tribe;

sentences.zh: 又次曰安居骨部；

translations.literal: next was the Anjugu tribe;
translations.idiomatic: Next came the Anjugu tribe;

sentences.zh: 益東曰拂涅部；

translations.literal: farther east was the Funie tribe;
translations.idiomatic: Farther east lay the Funie tribe;

sentences.zh: 居骨之西北曰黑水部；

translations.literal: northwest of Jugu was the Heishui tribe;
translations.idiomatic: Northwest of Jugu lay the Heishui tribe;

sentences.zh: 粟末之東曰白山部。

translations.literal: east of Sumo was the Baishan tribe.
translations.idiomatic: East of Sumo lay the Baishan tribe.

sentences.zh: 部間遠者三四百里，近二百里。

translations.literal: Between tribes the far were three or four hundred li, the near two hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: Between tribes the distant were three or four hundred li apart, the near two hundred.

sentences.zh: 白山本臣高麗，王師取平壤，其衆多入唐，汨咄、安居骨等皆奔散，浸微無聞焉，遺人迸入渤海。

translations.literal: Baishan had originally submitted to Goguryeo; when the imperial army took Pyongyang its multitude mostly entered Tang; Mizhu, Anjugu, and the rest all fled and scattered, gradually fading from record, and the remnant people rushed into Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: Baishan had originally submitted to Goguryeo. When the imperial army took Pyongyang most of its people entered Tang. Mizhu, Anjugu, and the rest all fled and scattered, gradually fading from record, and the remnant people rushed into Bohai.

sentences.zh: 唯黑水完強，分十六落，以南北稱，蓋其居最北方者也。

translations.literal: Only Heishui remained intact and strong, divided into sixteen settlements called north and south—they dwelt in the northernmost region.
translations.idiomatic: Only Heishui remained whole and strong, divided into sixteen settlements called north and south—they dwelt in the northernmost region.

sentences.zh: 人勁健，善步戰，常能患它部。

translations.literal: The people were stalwart and skilled at infantry fighting and could often trouble the other tribes.
translations.idiomatic: The people were hardy and skilled at infantry fighting and could often harry the other tribes.

sentences.zh: 俗編發，綴野豕牙，插雉尾爲冠飾，自別于諸部。

translations.literal: By custom they braided their hair, strung wild boar tusks, and inserted pheasant tails as crown ornaments to distinguish themselves from the other tribes.
translations.idiomatic: By custom they braided their hair, strung wild boar tusks, and wore pheasant tails in their crowns to set themselves apart from other tribes.

sentences.zh: 性忍悍，善射獵，無憂戚，貴壯賤老。

translations.literal: Their nature was enduring and fierce; they were skilled at shooting and hunting, without grief or worry, valuing the strong and despising the old.
