translations.idiomatic: Their nature was enduring and fierce. They were skilled at shooting and hunting, without grief or worry, valuing the strong and despising the old.

sentences.zh: 居無室廬，負山水坎地，梁木其上，覆以土，如丘塚然。

translations.literal: They had no houses or lodges but leaned on mountain streams in hollow ground, set beams atop, and covered with earth like a mound tomb.
translations.idiomatic: They built no fixed houses but leaned their dwellings on hollow ground beside mountain streams, set beams above, and covered them with earth like burial mounds.

sentences.zh: 夏出隨水草，冬入處。

translations.literal: In summer they went out following water and grass; in winter they entered their dwellings.
translations.idiomatic: In summer they followed water and grass; in winter they returned indoors.

sentences.zh: 以溺盥面，于夷狄最濁穢。

translations.literal: They washed the face with urine—the most filthy among the northern barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: They washed their faces with urine—regarded as the filthiest custom among the northern tribes.

sentences.zh: 死者埋之，無棺槨，殺所乘馬以祭。

translations.literal: The dead were buried without coffin or outer coffin, and the horse they had ridden was killed for sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: They buried the dead without coffins and killed the horse the deceased had ridden as an offering.

sentences.zh: 其酋曰大莫拂瞞咄，世相承爲長。

translations.literal: Their chief was called Damofumoduo, handed down generation after generation as leader.
translations.idiomatic: Their chief was called Damofumoduo, passed down generation after generation as leader.

sentences.zh: 無書契。

translations.literal: They had no writing or tallies.
translations.idiomatic: They had no writing or tallies.

sentences.zh: 其矢石鏃，長二寸，蓋楛砮遺法。

translations.literal: Their arrowheads were stone, two inches long—probably the legacy of the wooden-arrow method.
translations.idiomatic: Their arrowheads were stone, two inches long—probably a survival of the wooden-arrow tradition.

sentences.zh: 畜多豕，無牛羊。

translations.literal: Livestock was mostly swine; they had no cattle or sheep.
translations.idiomatic: They kept mostly pigs and had neither cattle nor sheep.

sentences.zh: 有車馬，田耦以耕，車則步推。

translations.literal: They had carts and horses; fields were tilled in pairs, and carts were pushed on foot.
translations.idiomatic: They had carts and horses, tilled fields in pairs, and pushed their carts on foot.

sentences.zh: 有粟麥。

translations.literal: They had millet and wheat.
translations.idiomatic: They had millet and wheat.

sentences.zh: 土多貂鼠、白兔、白鷹。

translations.literal: The land had much sable, rat, white hare, and white hawk.
translations.idiomatic: The land abounded in sable, rats, white hares, and white hawks.

sentences.zh: 有鹽泉，氣蒸薄，鹽凝樹顛。

translations.literal: There were salt springs; vapor steamed thinly and salt congealed atop the trees.
translations.idiomatic: Salt springs steamed thinly there, and salt congealed on the treetops.

sentences.zh: 武德五年，渠長阿固郎始來。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Wude the chieftain Agulang first came.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Wude the chieftain Agulang came for the first time.

sentences.zh: 太宗貞觀二年，乃臣附，所獻有常，以其地爲燕州。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenguan of Taizong they then submitted and presented regular tribute; their lands were made Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhenguan under Taizong they submitted, sent regular tribute, and their lands were made Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 帝伐高麗，其北部反，與高麗合。

translations.literal: When the Emperor campaigned against Goguryeo their northern tribes rebelled and joined with Goguryeo.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor campaigned against Goguryeo their northern tribes rebelled and joined with Goguryeo.

sentences.zh: 高惠真等率衆援安市，每戰，靺鞨常居前。

translations.literal: Gao Huizhen and others led troops to aid Anshi; in every battle the Mohe always went in the van.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huizhen and others led troops to relieve Anshi, and in every battle the Mohe fought in the van.

sentences.zh: 帝破安市，執惠真，收靺鞨兵三千餘，悉坑之。

translations.literal: When the Emperor broke Anshi he captured Huizhen and took more than three thousand Mohe soldiers, all buried alive.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor broke Anshi he captured Huizhen and took more than three thousand Mohe soldiers, all buried alive.

sentences.zh: 開元十年，其酋倪屬利稽來朝，玄宗即拜勃利州刺史。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Kaiyuan their chief Ni Shuliji came to court and Xuanzong at once appointed him prefect of Boli.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Kaiyuan their chief Ni Shuliji came to court, and Xuanzong immediately appointed him prefect of Boli.

sentences.zh: 於是安東都護薛泰請置黑水府，以部長爲都督、刺史，朝廷爲置長史監之，賜府都督姓李氏，名曰獻誠，以雲麾將軍領黑水經略使，隸幽州都督。

translations.literal: Then the Andong Protector Xue Tai requested establishment of the Heishui Prefecture, with tribal chiefs as protectors and prefects; the court set chief administrators to oversee them, granted the protector of the prefecture the surname Li and the name Xian Cheng, made Cloud-Banner General frontier commissioner of Heishui, subordinate to the Youzhou Protector.
translations.idiomatic: Then Andong Protector Xue Tai requested establishment of the Heishui Prefecture, with tribal chiefs as protectors and prefects. The court set chief administrators to oversee them, granted the prefecture protector the surname Li and the name Xian Cheng, made him Cloud-Banner General and frontier commissioner of Heishui, subordinate to the Youzhou protector.

sentences.zh: 訖帝世，朝獻者十五。

translations.literal: Through the whole of the Emperor’s reign they presented tribute fifteen times.
translations.idiomatic: Through the whole of the emperor’s reign they presented tribute fifteen times.

sentences.zh: 大曆世凡七，貞元一來，元和中再。

translations.literal: In the Dali era seven in all; in Zhenyuan one visit; in Yuanhe two.
translations.idiomatic: Seven visits in the Dali era, one in Zhenyuan, and two in Yuanhe.

sentences.zh: 初，黑水西北又有思慕部，益北行十日得郡利部，東北行十日得窟說部，亦號屈設，稍東南行十日得莫曳皆部，又有拂涅、虞婁、越喜、鐵利等部。

translations.literal: At first northwest of Heishui was also the Simu tribe; going north ten days more one reached the Junli tribe; going northeast ten days the Kushe tribe, also called Qushe; going somewhat southeast ten days the Moyijie tribe; there were also the Funie, Yulou, Yuexi, Tieli, and other tribes.
translations.idiomatic: At first northwest of Heishui was also the Simu tribe. Going north ten days more one reached the Junli tribe; going northeast ten days the Kushe tribe, also called Qushe; going somewhat southeast ten days the Moyijie tribe. There were also the Funie, Yulou, Yuexi, Tieli, and other tribes.

sentences.zh: 其地南距渤海，北、東際於海，西抵室韋，南北袤二千里，東西千里。

translations.literal: Their lands south bordered Bohai, north and east met the sea, west reached the Shiwei, two thousand li north to south and one thousand li east to west.
translations.idiomatic: Their lands bordered Bohai on the south, met the sea on the north and east, reached the Shiwei on the west—two thousand li north to south and one thousand li east to west.

sentences.zh: 拂涅、鐵利、虞婁、越喜時時通中國，而郡利，屈設、莫曳皆不能自通。

translations.literal: Funie, Tieli, Yulou, and Yuexi from time to time reached China, while Junli, Qushe, and Moyijie could not reach it on their own.
translations.idiomatic: Funie, Tieli, Yulou, and Yuexi reached China from time to time, while Junli, Qushe, and Moyijie could not do so on their own.

sentences.zh: 今存其朝京師者附左方。

translations.literal: Those now preserved who came to the capital are appended to the left section.
translations.idiomatic: Those of their envoys still recorded who came to the capital are appended in the left section.

sentences.zh: 拂涅，亦稱大拂涅，開元、天寶間八來，獻鯨睛、貂鼠、白兔皮；

translations.literal: Funie, also called Great Funie, came eight times between Kaiyuan and Tianbao, presenting whale eyes, sable, and white hare pelts;
translations.idiomatic: Funie, also called Great Funie, came eight times between Kaiyuan and Tianbao, presenting whale eyes, sable pelts, and white hare skins;

sentences.zh: 鐵利，開元中六來；

translations.literal: Tieli, six times in Kaiyuan;
translations.idiomatic: Tieli came six times in Kaiyuan;

sentences.zh: 越喜，七來，貞元中一來；

translations.literal: Yuexi, seven times, one in Zhenyuan;
translations.idiomatic: Yuexi came seven times, including once in Zhenyuan;

sentences.zh: 虞婁，貞觀間再來，貞元一來。

translations.literal: Yulou, twice in Zhenguan, once in Zhenyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Yulou came twice in Zhenguan and once in Zhenyuan.

sentences.zh: 後渤海盛，靺鞨皆役屬之，不復與王會矣。

translations.literal: Later Bohai grew strong and all the Mohe were made to serve and no longer attended court assemblies.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Bohai grew strong, all the Mohe were forced to serve them and no longer attended the Son of Heaven’s court.

sentences.zh: 渤海，本粟末靺鞨附高麗者，姓大氏。

translations.literal: Bohai were originally Sumo Mohe who had submitted to Goguryeo, surname Da.
translations.idiomatic: Bohai were originally Sumo Mohe who had submitted to Goguryeo, of the Da clan.

sentences.zh: 高麗滅，率衆保挹婁之東牟山，地直營州東二千里，南比新羅，以泥河爲境，東窮海，西契丹。

translations.literal: When Goguryeo perished they led the multitude to hold the eastern slopes of Mount Mou of Yilou, their lands straight two thousand li east of Yingzhou, south bordering Silla with the Ni River as boundary, east to the end of the sea, west the Khitan.
translations.idiomatic: When Goguryeo perished they led the multitude to hold the eastern slopes of Mount Mou of Yilou, their lands some two thousand li east of Yingzhou, bordering Silla on the south with the Ni River as boundary, east to the end of the sea, west the Khitan.

sentences.zh: 築城郭以居，高麗逋殘稍歸之。

translations.literal: They built walls and lodges to dwell; Goguryeo fugitive remnants gradually returned to them.
translations.idiomatic: They built walls and lodges to dwell, and Goguryeo fugitive remnants gradually returned to them.

sentences.zh: 萬歲通天中，契丹盡忠殺營州都督趙翽反，有舍利乞乞仲象者，與靺鞨酋乞四比羽及高麗餘種東走，度遼水，保太白山之東北，阻奧婁河，樹壁自固。

translations.literal: In the Wansui Tongtian era Jinzhong of the Khitan killed Youzhou Protector Zhao Wenshu and rebelled; there was one Qiqizhongxiang of the relics who, with the Mohe chief Qisi Biyu and Goguryeo remnants, fled east, crossed the Liao River, and held the northeast of Great White Mountain, blocking the Aolou River and building ramparts to secure themselves.
translations.idiomatic: In the Wansui Tongtian era Jinzhong of the Khitan killed Youzhou Protector Zhao Wenshu and rebelled. There was one Qiqizhongxiang of the relics who, with the Mohe chief Qisi Biyu and Goguryeo remnants, fled east, crossed the Liao River, and held the northeast of Great White Mountain, blocking the Aolou River and building ramparts to secure themselves.

sentences.zh: 武后封乞四比羽爲許國公，乞乞仲象爲震國公，赦其罪。

translations.literal: Empress Wu enfeoffed Qisi Biyu Duke of Xu and Qiqizhongxiang Duke of Zhen and pardoned their crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu enfeoffed Qisi Biyu as Duke of Xu and Qiqizhongxiang as Duke of Zhen and pardoned their crimes.

sentences.zh: 比羽不受命，后詔玉鈐衛大將軍李楷固、中郎將索仇擊斬之。

translations.literal: Biyu did not accept the command; the Empress ordered Jade-Clasp Guard Grand General Li Kailuo and Gentleman of the Palace Suo Chou to strike and behead him.
translations.idiomatic: Biyu did not accept the command. The empress ordered Jade-Clasp Guard Grand General Li Kailuo and Gentleman of the Palace Suo Chou to strike and behead him.

sentences.zh: 是時仲象已死，其子祚榮引殘痍遁去，楷固窮躡，度天門嶺。

translations.literal: At that time Zhongxiang was already dead; his son Zuorong led the wounded in flight and Kailuo pursued to the end, crossing Tianmen Ridge.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Zhongxiang was already dead. His son Zuorong led the wounded in flight and Kailuo pursued to the end, crossing Tianmen Ridge.

sentences.zh: 祚榮因高麗、靺鞨兵拒楷固，楷固敗還。

translations.literal: Zuorong relied on Goguryeo and Mohe troops to resist Kailuo, and Kailuo was defeated and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Zuorong used Goguryeo and Mohe troops to hold off Kailuo, who was beaten and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 於是契丹附突厥，王師道絕，不克討。

translations.literal: Then the Khitan submitted to the Turks and the imperial roads were cut off, and they could not be punished.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan then submitted to the Turks, imperial routes were cut, and the court could not punish them.

sentences.zh: 祚榮即並比羽之衆，恃荒遠，乃建國，自號震國王，遣使交突厥，地方五千里，戶十余萬，勝兵數萬。

translations.literal: Zuorong then merged Biyu’s multitude; relying on the remote wilds he established a state, styled himself King of Zhen, sent envoys to treat with the Turks, his territory five thousand li, households more than one hundred thousand, seasoned troops several tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Zuorong then merged Biyu’s multitude. Relying on the remote wilds he established a state, styled himself King of Zhen, sent envoys to treat with the Turks. His territory was five thousand li, households more than one hundred thousand, seasoned troops several tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 頗知書契，盡得扶餘、沃沮、弁韓、朝鮮海北諸國。

translations.literal: He was quite versed in writing and tallies and wholly obtained Fuyu, Woju, Byeonhan, and all the states north of the Korean seas.
translations.idiomatic: He was well versed in writing and tallies and wholly absorbed Fuyu, Woju, Byeonhan, and all the states north of the Korean seas.

sentences.zh: 中宗時，使侍御史張行岌招慰，祚榮遣子入侍。

translations.literal: In the Zhongzong era Attendant Censor Zhang Xingji was sent to summon and comfort them; Zuorong sent his son to serve at court.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhongzong era Attendant Censor Zhang Xingji was sent to summon and comfort them, and Zuorong sent his son to serve at court.

sentences.zh: 睿宗先天中，遣使拜祚榮爲左驍衛大將軍、渤海郡王，以所統爲忽汗州，領忽汗州都督。

translations.literal: In the Xiantian era of Ruizong envoys were sent to appoint Zuorong Left Valiant Cavalry Guard Grand General and Prince of Bohai, his domain made Hohan Prefecture, and he was made Protector of Hohan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the Xiantian era of Ruizong envoys were sent to appoint Zuorong Left Valiant Cavalry Guard Grand General and Prince of Bohai, his domain made Hohan Prefecture, and he was made protector of Hohan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 自是始去靺鞨號，專稱渤海。

translations.literal: From then they first dropped the Mohe name and called themselves only Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: From then on they dropped the Mohe name and called themselves only Bohai.

sentences.zh: 玄宗開元七年，祚榮死，其國私諡爲高王。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Kaiyuan of Xuanzong Zuorong died and his state privately posthumously styled him King Gao.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Kaiyuan under Xuanzong Zuorong died, and his state privately posthumously styled him King Gao.

sentences.zh: 子武藝立，斥大土宇，東北諸夷畏臣之，私改年曰仁安。

translations.literal: His son Wuyi stood, expanded the great territory, and the northeastern tribes all feared and submitted; he privately changed the era name to Ren’an.
translations.idiomatic: His son Wuyi succeeded, expanded the great territory, and the northeastern tribes all feared and submitted. He privately changed the era name to Ren’an.

sentences.zh: 帝賜典冊襲王並所領。

translations.literal: The Emperor bestowed the canonical patent to inherit the princely title and what he led.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor bestowed the canonical patent to inherit the princely title and what he led.

sentences.zh: 未幾，墨水靺鞨使者入朝，帝以其地建黑水州，置長史臨總。

translations.literal: Before long envoys of the Ink Mohe came to court and the Emperor made their lands Heishui Prefecture and set a chief administrator to oversee them in total.
translations.idiomatic: Before long envoys of the Ink Mohe came to court and the emperor made their lands Heishui Prefecture and set a chief administrator to oversee them in total.

sentences.zh: 武藝召其下謀曰：「黑水始假道于我與唐通，異時請吐屯於突厥，皆先告我，今請唐官不吾告，是必與唐腹背攻我也。

translations.literal: Wuyi summoned his subordinates to counsel, saying: “Heishui first borrowed our road to reach Tang. In other times when they asked the qaghan of the Turks for tutun, they always told us first. Now they ask Tang for officials without telling us—they must intend to attack us from front and back together with Tang.”
translations.idiomatic: Wuyi summoned his counselors and said: “Heishui first borrowed our road to reach Tang. Whenever they asked the Türk qaghan for tutun they always informed us first. Now they seek Tang offices without telling us—they must mean to strike us from front and rear together with Tang.”

sentences.zh: 」乃遣弟門藝及舅任雅相發兵擊黑水。

translations.literal: He then sent his younger brother Menyi and his maternal uncle Ren Yaxiang to mobilize troops and strike Heishui.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent his younger brother Menyi and his maternal uncle Ren Yaxiang to raise troops against Heishui.

sentences.zh: 門藝嘗質京師，知利害，謂武藝曰：「黑水請吏而我擊之，是背唐也。

translations.literal: Menyi had once been a hostage in the capital and knew advantage and harm; he told Wuyi: “Heishui asked for officials and we attack them—this is turning our back on Tang.”
translations.idiomatic: Menyi had once been a hostage in the capital and knew advantage and harm. He told Wuyi: “Heishui asked for officials and we attack them—this is turning our back on Tang.”

sentences.zh: 唐，大國，兵萬倍我，與之產怨，我且亡。

translations.literal: “Tang is a great state; its troops are ten thousand times ours. If we breed resentment with it, we shall perish.”
translations.idiomatic: “Tang is a great power; its armies outnumber ours ten thousandfold. If we earn its enmity, we are finished.”

sentences.zh: 昔高麗盛時，士三十萬，抗唐爲敵，可謂雄強，唐兵一臨，掃地盡矣。

translations.literal: “In the past when Goguryeo was strong it had three hundred thousand warriors and resisted Tang as an enemy—one may call that heroic strength; when Tang troops came once, they swept the ground clean.”
translations.idiomatic: “When Goguryeo was at its height it fielded three hundred thousand men and stood against Tang as an equal—truly formidable. Yet when Tang armies came once, they were swept away entirely.”

sentences.zh: 今我衆比高麗三之一，王將違之，不可。

translations.literal: “Now our multitude is one-third of Goguryeo’s; if Your Majesty goes against this, it cannot be done.”
translations.idiomatic: “Our forces today are only a third of Goguryeo’s. If Your Majesty goes against this counsel, it cannot be done.”

sentences.zh: 」武藝不從。

translations.literal: Wuyi would not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Wuyi refused to listen.

sentences.zh: 兵至境，又以書固諫。

translations.literal: When the army reached the border he again admonished by letter.
translations.idiomatic: When the army reached the border he wrote again in earnest protest.

sentences.zh: 武藝怒，遣從兄壹夏代將，召門藝，將殺之。

translations.literal: Wuyi was angry, sent his cousin Yixia to replace the commander, summoned Menyi, and meant to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Wuyi flew into a rage, sent his cousin Yixia to replace the commander, summoned Menyi, and intended to kill him.

sentences.zh: 門藝懼，儳路自歸，詔拜左驍衛將軍。

translations.literal: Menyi was afraid, took a bypath and came to submit; an edict appointed him Left Valiant Cavalry Guard General.
translations.idiomatic: Menyi was afraid, took a bypath and came to submit. An edict appointed him Left Valiant Cavalry Guard General.

sentences.zh: 武藝使使暴門藝罪惡，請誅之。

translations.literal: Wuyi sent envoys to expose Menyi’s crimes and ask that he be executed.
translations.idiomatic: Wuyi sent envoys denouncing Menyi’s crimes and asking that he be executed.

sentences.zh: 有詔處之安西，好報曰：「門藝窮來歸我，誼不可殺，已投之惡地。

translations.literal: There was an edict placing him in Anxi; a favorable reply said: “Menyi came in extremity to submit to us; by right he cannot be killed and has been cast into an evil land.”
translations.idiomatic: There was an edict placing him in Anxi. A favorable reply said: “Menyi came in extremity to submit to us; by right he cannot be killed and has been cast into an evil land.”

sentences.zh: 」並留使者不遣，別詔鴻臚少卿李道邃、源復諭旨。

translations.literal: The envoys were also detained and not sent back; a separate edict made Vice Director of the Court for Diplomatic Relations Li Daosui and Yuan Fu deliver the imperial intent.
translations.idiomatic: The envoys were also detained and not sent back. A separate edict made Vice Director of the Court for Diplomatic Relations Li Daosui and Yuan Fu deliver the imperial intent.

sentences.zh: 武藝知之，上書斥言：「陛下不當以妄示天下」，意必殺門藝。

translations.literal: When Wuyi learned of it he memorialized in rebuke: “Your Majesty ought not show the realm something false”—he meant certainly to kill Menyi.
translations.idiomatic: Learning of this, Wuyi memorialized in rebuke: “Your Majesty ought not deceive the realm”—he clearly meant to have Menyi killed.

sentences.zh: 帝怒道邃、復漏言國事，皆左除，而陽斥門藝以報。

translations.literal: The Emperor was angry that Daosui and Fu leaked state affairs; both were demoted to the left while openly rebuking Menyi in reply.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was angry that Daosui and Fu leaked state affairs. Both were demoted to the left while openly rebuking Menyi in reply.

sentences.zh: 後十年，武藝遣大將張文休率海賊攻登州，帝馳遣門藝發幽州兵擊之。

translations.literal: Ten years later Wuyi sent the great general Zhang Wenxiu leading sea raiders to attack Dengzhou; the Emperor urgently sent Menyi to mobilize Youzhou troops to strike them.
translations.idiomatic: Ten years later Wuyi sent the great general Zhang Wenxiu leading sea raiders to attack Dengzhou. The emperor urgently sent Menyi to mobilize Youzhou troops to strike them.

sentences.zh: 使太僕卿金思蘭使新羅，督兵攻其南。

translations.literal: He sent Minister of the Stud Jin Silan to Silla to supervise troops attacking their south.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Minister of the Stud Jin Silan to Silla to oversee an attack on their southern flank.

sentences.zh: 會大寒，雪袤丈，士凍死過半，無功而還。

translations.literal: It happened to be bitter cold; snow was one zhang deep; more than half the soldiers froze to death and they returned without merit.
translations.idiomatic: Bitter cold set in; snow lay a zhang deep; more than half the troops froze to death, and the campaign returned without success.

sentences.zh: 武藝望其弟不已，募客入東都狙刺於道。

translations.literal: Wuyi longed for his younger brother without cease and recruited agents to enter the eastern capital to ambush him on the road.
translations.idiomatic: Wuyi could not stop longing for his brother and hired agents to ambush him on the road into the eastern capital.

sentences.zh: 門藝格之，得不死。

translations.literal: Menyi parried them and did not die.
translations.idiomatic: Menyi parried the blow and survived.

sentences.zh: 河南捕刺客，悉殺之。

translations.literal: Henan captured the assassins and killed them all.
translations.idiomatic: Henan arrested the assassins and executed them all.

sentences.zh: 武藝死，其國私諡武王。

translations.literal: When Wuyi died his state privately posthumously styled him King Wu.
translations.idiomatic: When Wuyi died his state privately posthumously styled him King Wu.

sentences.zh: 子欽茂立，改年大興，有詔嗣王及所領，欽茂因是赦境內。

translations.literal: His son Qinmao stood, changed the era name to Daxing, and there was an edict that he inherit the princely title and what he led; Qinmao therefore amnestied within the borders.
translations.idiomatic: His son Qinmao succeeded, changed the era name to Daxing, and there was an edict that he inherit the princely title and what he led. Qinmao therefore amnestied within the borders.

sentences.zh: 天寶末，欽茂徙上京，直舊國三百里忽汗河之東。

translations.literal: At the end of Tianbao Qinmao moved the upper capital, straight three hundred li from the old state east of the Hohan River.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Tianbao Qinmao moved the upper capital, some three hundred li from the old state east of the Hohan River.

sentences.zh: 訖帝世，朝獻者二十九。

translations.literal: Through the whole of the Emperor’s reign they presented tribute twenty-nine times.
translations.idiomatic: Through the whole of the emperor’s reign they presented tribute twenty-nine times.

sentences.zh: 寶應元年，詔以渤海爲國，欽茂王之，進檢校太尉。

translations.literal: In the first year of Baoying an edict made Bohai a state; Qinmao was made its king and promoted Inspector-in-Chief Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Baoying an edict made Bohai a kingdom; Qinmao was crowned its king and promoted Inspector-in-Chief Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 大曆中，二十五來，以日本舞女十一獻諸朝。

translations.literal: In the Dali era they came twenty-five times, presenting eleven Japanese dancing girls to the court.
translations.idiomatic: In the Dali era they came twenty-five times, once presenting eleven Japanese dancing girls to the court.

sentences.zh: 貞元時，東南徙東京。

translations.literal: In the Zhenyuan era they moved southeast to the eastern capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhenyuan era they moved southeast to the eastern capital.

sentences.zh: 欽茂死，私諡文王。

translations.literal: When Qinmao died he was privately posthumously styled King Wen.
translations.idiomatic: When Qinmao died he was privately posthumously styled King Wen.

sentences.zh: 子宏臨早死，族弟元義立一歲，猜虐，國人殺之。

translations.literal: His son Honglin died early; clansman Yuan Yi stood one year, was suspicious and cruel, and the people killed him.
translations.idiomatic: His son Honglin died early. Clansman Yuan Yi reigned one year, proved suspicious and cruel, and the people killed him.

sentences.zh: 推宏臨子華璵爲王，復還上京，改年中興。

translations.literal: They pushed Honglin’s son Hua Yu to be king, returned to the upper capital, and changed the era name to Zhongxing.
translations.idiomatic: They set Honglin’s son Hua Yu on the throne, returned to the upper capital, and changed the era name to Zhongxing.

sentences.zh: 死，諡曰成王。

translations.literal: When he died he was posthumously styled King Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he received the posthumous title King Cheng.

sentences.zh: 欽茂少子嵩鄰立，改年正曆，有詔授右驍衛大將軍，嗣王。

translations.literal: Qinmao’s youngest son Songlin stood, changed the era name to Zhengli, and there was an edict appointing him Right Valiant Cavalry Guard Grand General and successor to the princely title.
translations.idiomatic: Qinmao’s youngest son Songlin succeeded, changed the era name to Zhengli, and an edict appointed him Right Valiant Cavalry Guard Grand General and successor to the princely title.

sentences.zh: 建中、貞元間凡四來。

translations.literal: Between Jianzhong and Zhenyuan they came four times in all.
translations.idiomatic: Between Jianzhong and Zhenyuan they came four times in all.

sentences.zh: 死，諡康王。

translations.literal: When he died he was posthumously styled King Kang.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he was posthumously styled King Kang.

sentences.zh: 子元瑜立，改年永德。

translations.literal: His son Yuanyu stood and changed the era name to Yongde.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yuanyu succeeded and changed the era name to Yongde.

sentences.zh: 死，諡定王。

translations.literal: When he died he was posthumously styled King Ding.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he was posthumously styled King Ding.

sentences.zh: 弟言義立，改年硃雀，並襲王如故事。

translations.literal: His younger brother Yanyi stood, changed the era name to Zhuque, and inherited the princely title as before.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Yanyi succeeded, changed the era name to Zhuque, and inherited the princely title as before.

sentences.zh: 死，諡僖王。

translations.literal: When he died he was posthumously styled King Xi.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he was posthumously styled King Xi.

sentences.zh: 弟明忠立，改年太始，立一歲死，諡簡王。

translations.literal: His younger brother Mingzhong stood, changed the era name to Taishi, stood one year and died, posthumously styled King Jian.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Mingzhong succeeded, changed the era name to Taishi, reigned one year and died, and was posthumously styled King Jian.

sentences.zh: 從父仁秀立，改年建興，其四世祖野勃，祚榮弟也。

translations.literal: His cousin on the father’s side Renxiu stood, changed the era name to Jianxing; his fourth-generation ancestor Yebo was Zuorong’s younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: His cousin on the father’s side Renxiu succeeded and changed the era name to Jianxing. His fourth-generation ancestor Yebo was Zuorong’s younger brother.

sentences.zh: 仁秀頗能討伐海北諸部，開大境宇，有功，詔檢校司空、襲王。

translations.literal: Renxiu was quite able in campaigning against the tribes north of the sea, opened a great territory, and had merit; an edict made him Acting Minister of Works and successor to the princely title.
translations.idiomatic: Renxiu was quite able in campaigning against the tribes north of the sea, opened a great territory, and won merit. An edict made him Acting Minister of Works and successor to the princely title.

sentences.zh: 元和中，凡十六朝獻，長慶四，寶曆凡再。

translations.literal: In the Yuanhe era they presented tribute sixteen times in all; in Changqing four; in Baoli twice in all.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanhe they presented tribute sixteen times; in Changqing four; in Baoli twice.

sentences.zh: 大和四年，仁秀死，諡宣王。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Dahe Renxiu died and was posthumously styled King Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Dahe Renxiu died and was posthumously styled King Xuan.

sentences.zh: 子新德蚤死，孫彝震立，改年鹹和。

translations.literal: His son Xinde died early and his grandson Yizhen stood, changing the era name to Xianhe.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xinde died early and his grandson Yizhen succeeded, changing the era name to Xianhe.

sentences.zh: 明年，詔襲爵。

translations.literal: The next year an edict granted succession to the title.
translations.idiomatic: The next year an edict confirmed his succession to the title.

sentences.zh: 終文宗世來朝十二，會昌凡四。

translations.literal: Through the whole of Wenzong’s reign they came to court twelve times; in Huichang four in all.
translations.idiomatic: Through Wenzong’s entire reign they came to court twelve times; in Huichang four times in all.

sentences.zh: 彝震死，弟虔晃立。

translations.literal: When Yizhen died his younger brother Qianhuang stood.
translations.idiomatic: When Yizhen died his younger brother Qianhuang succeeded.

sentences.zh: 死，玄錫立。

translations.literal: When he died Xuanxi stood.
translations.idiomatic: When he died Xuanxi succeeded.

sentences.zh: 咸通時，三朝獻。

translations.literal: In the Xiantong era they presented tribute three times.
translations.idiomatic: In the Xiantong era they presented tribute three times.

sentences.zh: 初，其王數遣諸生詣京師太學，習識古今制度，至是遂爲海東盛國，地有五京、十五府、六十二州。

translations.literal: At first their kings repeatedly sent students to the Imperial University in the capital to study ancient and modern institutions; by then they had become the flourishing state east of the sea, their lands having five capitals, fifteen prefectures, and sixty-two districts.
translations.idiomatic: At first their kings repeatedly sent students to the Imperial University in the capital to study ancient and modern institutions. By then they had become the flourishing state east of the sea, with five capitals, fifteen prefectures, and sixty-two districts.

sentences.zh: 以肅慎故地爲上京，曰龍泉府，領龍、湖、渤三州。

translations.literal: The old Sushhen lands were made the upper capital, called Longquan Prefecture, overseeing Long, Hu, and Bo districts.
translations.idiomatic: The old Sushhen lands became the upper capital, called Longquan Prefecture, with Long, Hu, and Bo districts under it.

sentences.zh: 其南爲中京，曰顯德府，領廬、顯、鐵、湯、榮、興六州。

translations.literal: To its south was the central capital, called Xiande Prefecture, overseeing Lu, Xian, Tie, Tang, Rong, and Xing—six districts.
translations.idiomatic: To the south stood the central capital, Xiande Prefecture, governing six districts: Lu, Xian, Tie, Tang, Rong, and Xing.

sentences.zh: 𧴖貃故地爲東京，曰龍原府，亦曰柵城府，領慶、鹽、穆、賀四州。

translations.literal: The old Mohe lands were made the eastern capital, called Longyuan Prefecture, also called Zhaicheng Prefecture, overseeing Qing, Yan, Mu, and He—four districts.
translations.idiomatic: The old Mohe lands became the eastern capital, Longyuan Prefecture—also called Zhaicheng Prefecture—with four districts: Qing, Yan, Mu, and He.

sentences.zh: 沃沮故地爲南京，曰南海府，領沃、睛、椒三州。

translations.literal: The old Woju lands were made the southern capital, called Nanhai Prefecture, overseeing Wo, Jing, and Jiao—three districts.
translations.idiomatic: The old Woju lands became the southern capital, Nanhai Prefecture, with three districts: Wo, Jing, and Jiao.

sentences.zh: 高麗故地爲西京，曰鴨淥府，領神、桓、豐、正四州；

translations.literal: The old Goguryeo lands were made the western capital, called Yalu Prefecture, overseeing Shen, Huan, Feng, and Zheng—four districts;
translations.idiomatic: The old Goguryeo lands became the western capital, Yalu Prefecture, with four districts: Shen, Huan, Feng, and Zheng;

sentences.zh: 曰長嶺府，領瑕、河二州。

translations.literal: called Changling Prefecture, overseeing Xia and He—two districts.
translations.idiomatic: and Changling Prefecture, with Xia and He districts.

sentences.zh: 扶餘故地爲扶餘府，常屯勁兵扞契丹，領扶、仙二州；

translations.literal: The old Fuyu lands were made Fuyu Prefecture, constantly garrisoning crack troops to hold the Khitan, overseeing Fu and Xian—two districts;
translations.idiomatic: The old Fuyu lands became Fuyu Prefecture, garrisoning crack troops against the Khitan, with Fu and Xian districts;

sentences.zh: 鄚頡府領鄚、高二州。

translations.literal: Mojie Prefecture oversaw Mo and Gao—two districts.
translations.idiomatic: Mojie Prefecture governed Mo and Gao districts.

sentences.zh: 挹婁故地爲定理府，領定、潘二州；

translations.literal: The old Yilou lands were made Dingli Prefecture, overseeing Ding and Pan—two districts;
translations.idiomatic: The old Yilou lands became Dingli Prefecture, with Ding and Pan districts;

sentences.zh: 安邊府領安、瓊二州。

translations.literal: Anbian Prefecture oversaw An and Qiong—two districts.
translations.idiomatic: Anbian Prefecture governed An and Qiong districts.

sentences.zh: 率賓故地爲率賓府，領華、益、建三州。

translations.literal: The old Shuaibin lands were made Shuaibin Prefecture, overseeing Hua, Yi, and Jian—three districts.
translations.idiomatic: The old Shuaibin lands became Shuaibin Prefecture, with Hua, Yi, and Jian districts.

sentences.zh: 拂涅故地爲東平府，領伊、蒙、沱、黑、比五州。

translations.literal: The old Funie lands were made Dongping Prefecture, overseeing Yi, Meng, Tuo, Hei, and Bi—five districts.
translations.idiomatic: The old Funie lands became Dongping Prefecture, with Yi, Meng, Tuo, Hei, and Bi districts.

sentences.zh: 鐵利故地爲鐵利府，領廣、汾、蒲、海、義、歸六州。

translations.literal: The old Tieli lands were made Tieli Prefecture, overseeing Guang, Fen, Pu, Hai, Yi, and Gui—six districts.
translations.idiomatic: The old Tieli lands became Tieli Prefecture, with Guang, Fen, Pu, Hai, Yi, and Gui districts.

sentences.zh: 越喜故地爲懷遠府，領達、越、懷、紀、富、美、福、邪、芝九州；

translations.literal: The old Yuexi lands were made Huaiyuan Prefecture, overseeing Da, Yue, Huai, Ji, Fu, Mei, Fu, Xie, and Zhi—nine districts;
translations.idiomatic: The old Yuexi lands became Huaiyuan Prefecture, with nine districts: Da, Yue, Huai, Ji, Fu, Mei, Fu, Xie, and Zhi;

sentences.zh: 安遠府領寧、郿、慕、常四州。

translations.literal: Anyuan Prefecture oversaw Ning, Mei, Mu, and Chang—four districts.
translations.idiomatic: Anyuan Prefecture governed Ning, Mei, Mu, and Chang districts.

sentences.zh: 又郢、銅、涑三州爲獨奏州。

translations.literal: Further the three districts of Ying, Tong, and Su were sole memorial districts.
translations.idiomatic: Ying, Tong, and Su districts were reserved for direct memorials to the throne.

sentences.zh: 涑州以其近涑沫江，蓋所謂粟末水也。

translations.literal: Su District because it was near the Sumo River—probably what was called the Sumo River.
translations.idiomatic: Su District lay near the Sumo River—probably what was called the Sumo River.

sentences.zh: 龍原東南瀕海，日本道也。

translations.literal: Longyuan southeast bordered the sea—the road to Japan.
translations.idiomatic: Southeast of Longyuan lay the sea—the route to Japan.

sentences.zh: 南海，新羅道也。

translations.literal: Nanhai—the road to Silla.
translations.idiomatic: Nanhai marked the route to Silla.

sentences.zh: 鴨淥，朝貢道也。

translations.literal: Yalu—the tribute road.
translations.idiomatic: Yalu was the tribute route.

sentences.zh: 長嶺，營州道也。

translations.literal: Changling—the road to Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Changling was the route to Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 扶餘，契丹道也。

translations.literal: Fuyu—the road to the Khitan.
translations.idiomatic: Fuyu was the route to the Khitan.

sentences.zh: 俗謂王曰「可毒夫」，曰「聖王」，曰「基下」。

translations.literal: By custom they called the king “Kedu Fu,” “Holy King,” and “Beneath the Foundation.”
translations.idiomatic: By custom they addressed the king as “Kedu Fu,” “Holy King,” and “Beneath the Foundation.”

sentences.zh: 其命爲「教」。

translations.literal: His commands were called “teachings.”
translations.idiomatic: His commands were styled “teachings.”

sentences.zh: 王之父曰「老王」，母「太妃」，妻「貴妃」，長子曰「副王」，諸子曰「王子」。

translations.literal: The king’s father was called “Old King,” the mother “Great Consort,” the wife “Honored Consort,” the eldest son “Deputy King,” and the other sons “Princes.”
translations.idiomatic: The king’s father was “Old King,” his mother “Great Consort,” his wife “Honored Consort,” his eldest son “Deputy King,” and his other sons “Princes.”

sentences.zh: 官有宣詔省，左相、左平章事、侍中、左常侍、諫議居之。

translations.literal: Offices included the Proclamation Bureau, with Left Chancellor, Left Associate Chancellor, Attendant-in-Chief, Left Regular Attendant, and Remonstrator.
translations.idiomatic: Offices included the Proclamation Bureau, housing the Left Chancellor, Left Associate Chancellor, Attendant-in-Chief, Left Regular Attendant, and Remonstrator.

sentences.zh: 中台省，右相、右平章事、內史、詔誥舍人居之。

translations.literal: The Central Terrace Bureau, with Right Chancellor, Right Associate Chancellor, Grand Secretary, and Edict Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: The Central Terrace Bureau held the Right Chancellor, Right Associate Chancellor, Grand Secretary, and Edict Drafter.

sentences.zh: 政堂省，大內相一人，居左右相上；

translations.literal: The Governance Hall Bureau had one Grand Inner Chancellor above the Left and Right Chancellors;
translations.idiomatic: The Governance Hall Bureau had one Grand Inner Chancellor above the Left and Right Chancellors;

sentences.zh: 左、右司政各一，居左右平章事之下，以比僕射；

translations.literal: Left and Right Directors of Governance each one, below the Left and Right Associate Chancellors, comparable to vice premiers;
translations.idiomatic: a Left and a Right Director of Governance, each below the associate chancellors and comparable to vice premiers;

sentences.zh: 左、右允比二丞。

translations.literal: Left and Right Assistants comparable to the two vice directors.
translations.idiomatic: and Left and Right Assistants comparable to the two vice directors.

sentences.zh: 左六司，忠、仁、義部各一卿，居司政下，支司爵、倉、膳部，部有郎中、員外；

translations.literal: The Left Six Bureaus: Loyalty, Benevolence, and Righteousness departments each with one director below the Directors of Governance; sub-bureaus of Enfeoffment, Granary, and Provisions departments, each department with Director and Vice Director;
translations.idiomatic: The Left Six Bureaus—Loyalty, Benevolence, and Righteousness—each had a director under the Directors of Governance, with sub-bureaus for Enfeoffment, Granary, and Provisions, each with a director and vice director;

sentences.zh: 右六司，智、禮、信部，支司戎、計、水部，卿、郎准左：以比六官。

translations.literal: the Right Six Bureaus: Wisdom, Rites, and Trust departments; sub-bureaus of Military, Accounts, and Water departments; directors and vice directors matching the left—comparable to the Six Offices.
translations.idiomatic: the Right Six Bureaus—Wisdom, Rites, and Trust—with Military, Accounts, and Water sub-bureaus, their directors matching the left in rank, modeled on the Six Offices.

sentences.zh: 中正台，大中正一，比御史大夫，居司政下；

translations.literal: The Central Rectitude Bureau had one Grand Rectifier comparable to Censor-in-Chief below the Directors of Governance;
translations.idiomatic: The Central Rectitude Bureau had one Grand Rectifier, comparable to Censor-in-Chief, below the Directors of Governance;

sentences.zh: 少正一。

translations.literal: one Vice Rectifier.
translations.idiomatic: one Vice Rectifier.

sentences.zh: 又有殿中寺、宗屬寺，有大令。

translations.literal: There were also the Palace Bureau and the Clan Relations Bureau, each with a Grand Director.
translations.idiomatic: There were also the Palace Bureau and the Clan Relations Bureau, each headed by a Grand Director.

sentences.zh: 文籍院有監。

translations.literal: The Documents Bureau had a Supervisor.
translations.idiomatic: The Documents Bureau had a Supervisor.

sentences.zh: 令、監皆有少。

translations.literal: Directors and supervisors all had deputies.
translations.idiomatic: Every director and supervisor had a deputy.

sentences.zh: 太常、司賓、大農寺，寺有卿。

translations.literal: The Grand Sacrifices, Guest Relations, and Agriculture Bureaus each had a Director.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Sacrifices, Guest Relations, and Agriculture Bureaus each had a director.

sentences.zh: 司藏、司膳寺，寺有令、丞。

translations.literal: The Treasury and Provisions Bureaus each had Director and Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: The Treasury and Provisions Bureaus each had a director and vice director.

sentences.zh: 胄子監有監長。

translations.literal: The Crown Prince’s College had a Chief Supervisor.
translations.idiomatic: The Crown Prince’s College had a chief supervisor.

sentences.zh: 巷伯局有常侍等官。

translations.literal: The Palace Steward Bureau had Regular Attendants and other officials.
translations.idiomatic: The Palace Steward Bureau included Regular Attendants and other officers.

sentences.zh: 其武員有左右猛賁、熊衛、羆衛，南左右衛，北左右衛，各大將軍一、將軍一。

translations.literal: Their military officers included Left and Right Fierce Guards, Bear Guards, and Panda Guards; South Left and Right Guards and North Left and Right Guards, each with one Grand General and one General.
translations.idiomatic: Their military ranks included Left and Right Fierce Guards, Bear Guards, and Panda Guards, and South and North Left and Right Guards, each with one grand general and one general.

sentences.zh: 大抵憲象中國制度如此。

translations.literal: On the whole they modeled the institutions of China in this way.
translations.idiomatic: In general their institutions mirrored those of China in this fashion.

sentences.zh: 以品爲秩，三秩以上服紫，牙笏、金魚。

translations.literal: Ranks were taken as grades; third rank and above wore purple, ivory tablet, and gold fish.
translations.idiomatic: Ranks served as grades: third rank and above wore purple robes, ivory tablets, and gold fish tokens.

sentences.zh: 五秩以上服緋，牙笏、銀魚。

translations.literal: Fifth rank and above wore scarlet, ivory tablet, and silver fish.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth rank and above wore scarlet, ivory tablets, and silver fish tokens.

sentences.zh: 六秩、七秩淺緋衣，八秩綠衣，皆木笏。

translations.literal: Sixth and seventh ranks wore light scarlet; eighth rank green; all had wooden tablets.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth and seventh ranks wore pale scarlet; eighth rank green; all carried wooden tablets.

sentences.zh: 俗所貴者，曰太白山之菟，南海之昆布，柵城之豉，扶餘之鹿，鄚頡之豕，率賓之馬，顯州之布，沃州之綿，龍州之紬，位城之鐵，廬城之稻，湄沱湖之鯽。

translations.literal: What their custom prized: hares of Great White Mountain, kelp of the southern sea, fermented beans of Zhaicheng, deer of Fuyu, swine of Mojie, horses of Shuaibin, cloth of Xian District, cotton of Wo District, silk of Long District, iron of Weicheng, rice of Lucheng, crucian carp of Meituo Lake.
translations.idiomatic: Their prized products included hares of Great White Mountain, kelp from the southern sea, fermented beans of Zhaicheng, deer of Fuyu, swine of Mojie, horses of Shuaibin, cloth of Xian District, cotton of Wo District, silk of Long District, iron of Weicheng, rice of Lucheng, and crucian carp of Meituo Lake.

sentences.zh: 果有九都之李，樂遊之梨。

translations.literal: Fruits included plums of Jiudu and pears of Leyou.
translations.idiomatic: Among their fruits were plums of Jiudu and pears of Leyou.

sentences.zh: 餘俗與高麗、契丹略等。

translations.literal: The rest of their customs were roughly equal to Goguryeo and the Khitan.
translations.idiomatic: Their remaining customs were much like those of Goguryeo and the Khitan.

sentences.zh: 幽州節度府與相聘問，自營、平距京師蓋八千里而遠。

translations.literal: The Youzhou frontier command exchanged envoys with them; from Ying and Ping to the capital was probably eight thousand li distant.
translations.idiomatic: The Youzhou frontier command exchanged envoys with them. From Ying and Ping to the capital was probably eight thousand li distant.

sentences.zh: 後朝貢至否，史家失傳，故叛附無考焉。

translations.literal: Later whether tribute came to court is lost in the historians’ record, and thus rebellion and submission cannot be examined.
translations.idiomatic: Later whether they continued tribute is lost in the historians’ record, so their rebellions and submissions cannot be traced.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：唐之德大矣！

translations.literal: The commentator says: How great was Tang’s virtue!
translations.idiomatic: The commentator says: How vast was Tang’s virtue!

sentences.zh: 際天所覆，悉臣而屬之；

translations.literal: All that the sky covers submitted and attached themselves;
translations.idiomatic: All beneath Heaven’s cover submitted and attached themselves to it;

sentences.zh: 薄海內外，無不州縣，遂尊天子曰「天可汗」。

translations.literal: within the near sea and beyond, none were without prefectures and districts, and thus the Son of Heaven was honored as “Heavenly Qaghan.”
translations.idiomatic: within the seas and beyond, none lacked prefectures and districts, and so the Son of Heaven was honored as “Heavenly Qaghan.”

sentences.zh: 三王以來，未有以過之。

translations.literal: Since the Three Dynasties there had been none to surpass it.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Three Dynasties none had surpassed it.

sentences.zh: 至荒區君長，待唐璽纛乃能國；

translations.literal: Even frontier chieftains could hold their states only after awaiting Tang’s seals and banners;
translations.idiomatic: Even chieftains of the wild borderlands could rule only after receiving Tang’s seals and banners;

sentences.zh: 一爲不賓，隨輒夷縛。

translations.literal: once they were not submissive, they were promptly bound and extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: once they refused submission, they were swiftly bound and destroyed.

sentences.zh: 故蠻琛夷寶，踵相逮於廷。

translations.literal: Thus barbarian treasures and outer tribute followed one another in succession at court.
translations.idiomatic: Thus barbarian treasures and outer tribute followed one another in endless succession at court.

sentences.zh: 極熾而衰，厥禍內移，天寶之後，區夏痍破，王官之戍，北不逾河，西止秦、邠，淩夷百年，逮于亡，顧不痛哉！

translations.literal: At the height of splendor they declined; the calamity shifted inward; after Tianbao the realm was wounded and broken, the garrisons of the king’s officers north of the river no more, west only to Qin and Bin—declining for a hundred years until perishing—how can one not grieve!
translations.idiomatic: At the height of splendor they declined; the calamity shifted inward. After Tianbao the realm was wounded and broken; the king’s garrisons north of the river advanced no more, west only to Qin and Bin—declining for a hundred years until perishing. How can one not grieve!

sentences.zh: 故曰：治己治人，惟聖人能之。

translations.literal: Therefore it is said: To govern oneself and govern others—only the sage can do it.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore it is said: To govern oneself and govern others is a task only the sage can perform.
